steps.body: The position response also equals \(P^a_t=\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}W^a_sds\), hence \(V^a_t=W^a_t-\gamma\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}W^a_sds\). To prove this for the exact translated construction, Lean pulls the established unshifted formula back through the injective isonormal isometry, then sends the deterministic identity through the translated continuous linear map. Continuity ensures Bochner integrability. Commuting that map with the integral and its scalar factors yields the formula; the velocity version follows by the balance identity. These are exact integration-by-parts identities on the constructed Brownian source.

KineticLangevin/MildEquation.lean.title: From the actual integral equation to the exponential mild equation
KineticLangevin/MildEquation.lean.summary: The KLMC update freezes the force inside an exponentially weighted integral. To compare it with an exact path, that weighted formula must follow from the actual integral equation driven by the same Brownian input. The theorem below proves this bridge for any complete real normed space, including the L² space of random Euclidean vectors. No time derivative of Brownian motion is used.

steps.title: Subtract the filtered noise and apply an integrating factor
steps.body: Assume continuous velocity \(V\), continuous force path \(F\), and a continuous filtered input \(B\), satisfying \(V_t-V_0=-\int_0^t(\gamma V_s+F_s)ds+W_t\) and \(B_t=W_t-\gamma\int_0^tB_sds\). The conclusion is the exact identity \(V_T=e^{-\gamma T}V_0-\int_0^Te^{-\gamma(T-s)}F_sds+B_T\). In the proof, evaluation at zero first gives \(B_0=0\). Subtracting the two equations shows \(D=V-B\) solves \(D_t=V_0-\int_0^t(\gamma D_s+F_s)ds\). Continuous integrands allow the fundamental theorem of calculus on the interval interior. Lean derives \(D\!\prime=-\gamma D-F\), differentiates \(e^{\gamma t}D_t\), and obtains derivative \(-e^{\gamma t}F_t\). A second application of the fundamental theorem integrates this identity over the closed interval; the proof handles the endpoints by continuity. Finally it multiplies by \(e^{-\gamma T}\), commutes scalar multiplication with the Bochner integral, and simplifies the exponent. The hypotheses are the genuine integral equations, and the resulting mild equation is proved rather than postulated. The argument works for arbitrary real friction and includes \(T=0\).

KineticLangevin/OBABORemainder.lean.title: OBABO: controlling every discrete remainder in the weighted metric
KineticLangevin/OBABORemainder.lean.summary: This module proves the numerical heart of the OBABO synchronous contraction. Starting from the explicit two-kick map, it bounds the averaged-force sector error, the Euler drift, and both components of the discrete remainder. These estimates combine to give the source factor \(1-mh/(3\gamma)\) under \(33\gamma^3h\le m\). The actual gradient and exponential damping are instantiated in the next module.

steps.title: Realize the modified energy as an ordinary Hilbert norm
steps.body: Complete the square: \(E_{a,b}(v,x)=\|x+bv\|^2+(a-b^2)\|v\|^2\). The map \((v,x)\mapsto(x+bv,\sqrt{a-b^2}v)\) lands in the Euclidean product WithLp 2. This explicit choice matters: the ordinary Lean product norm is a maximum norm. weightedPhaseNorm_sq expands the two component norms, uses the square-root identity for nonnegative \(a-b^2\), and normalizes the scalar algebra. The associated bilinear pairing is exactly the Euclidean inner product of these transforms, so its upper bound follows from Cauchy–Schwarz without an extra geometric assumption.

steps.title: Expand the exact energy of an Euler step plus a residual
steps.body: Expand \(E(s+t)=E(s)+2B(s,t)+E(t)\) and \(E(ct)=c^2E(t)\) directly from norms and inner products. Cauchy–Schwarz and \((\|s\|_E-\|t\|_E)^2\ge0\) give \(E(s+t)\le2E(s)+2E(t)\). For \(s_{+}=s+hA+r\), retain the first-order pairing \(2hB(s,A)\), bound the initial-residual pairing by \(2\|s\|_E\|r\|_E\), and apply the two-term estimate only to \(hA+r\). The resulting explicit bound is \(E(s_+)\le E(s)+2hB(s,A)+2\|s\|_E\|r\|_E+2h^2E(A)+2E(r)\). For the kinetic drift \(A=(-\gamma v-F,v)\), Lean checks that \(2B(s,A)\) is precisely the continuous derivative formula in the preceding module.

steps.title: Bound the drift and residual using their actual components
steps.body: The averaged force obeys the explicit envelope \(\|F\|\le17L\|x\|/16+\gamma\|v\|/8\). Expanding the drift energy and using the nonnegative square \((\gamma\|x\|-2\|v\|)^2\) bounds its mixed term. The friction condition \(4L\le\gamma^2\) and metric equivalence then give \(E(A)\le13\gamma^2E(s)/4\). For the residual, assume only the directly verifiable component bounds \(\|r_x\|\le h^2(\gamma\|v\|+L\|x\|)/2\) and \(\|r_v\|\le h^2(9\gamma L\|x\|/16+5\gamma^2\|v\|/8)\). Squaring each envelope uses \((a-b)^2\ge0\); multiplying by positive coefficients preserves the inequalities. Metric equivalence and \(4L\le\gamma^2\) yield \(E(r)\le3h^4\gamma^4E(s)\). No norm error estimate is supplied as a convergence hypothesis.

steps.title: Pay for the approximate centered sector
steps.body: The actual change in position gives \(e\le hL(\|v\|/2+\gamma\|x\|/16)\). The continuous dissipativity therefore contributes the positive correction \(h(2e\|x\|/\gamma+e^2/(\gamma L))\). The proof bounds \(e^2\) with the square of the difference of its two summands, and bounds the position-velocity term using \((\gamma\|x\|-2\|v\|)^2\). The restrictions \(\gamma h\le1\), \(4L\le\gamma^2\), together with the lower metric equivalence, give the explicit budget \(\gamma^2h^2E(s)/2\). Denominators are cleared only with positive factors; the remaining scalar inequalities are checked by Lean arithmetic.

steps.title: Recover the source step-size constant from the complete budget
steps.body:
The residual energy bound implies \(\|r\|_E\le7h^2\gamma^2\|s\|_E/4\), since \(\sqrt3\le7/4\). Thus the initial-residual cross term costs at most \(7\gamma^2h^2E(s)/2\). The drift term costs \(13\gamma^2h^2E(s)/2\), the sector correction costs \(\gamma^2h^2E(s)/2\), and \(12\gamma^2h^2\le1\) makes twice the residual energy cost at most another \(\gamma^2h^2E(s)/2\). Their sum is exactly \(11\gamma^2h^2E(s)\). Consequently the map contracts by \(1-2mh/(3\gamma)+11\gamma^2h^2\), which is at most \(1-mh/(3\gamma)\) when \(33\gamma^3h\le m\).

The final algebra theorem constructs the residual explicitly: \(r_x=h(\delta-1)v-h^2F_0/2\), \(r_v=(\delta^2-1+\gamma h)v+h(1-\delta)F\). Norm triangle inequalities and the damping envelopes prove the two component bounds internally. The identity between \(s+hA+r\) and the actual difference update is checked by module, so no update-error contract is assumed.

KineticLangevin/ProductLaw.lean.title: Actual KLMC output laws on concrete initial-coupling extensions
KineticLangevin/ProductLaw.lean.summary: An estimate for one coupling must eventually be optimized over all initial couplings. Its numerical output law must therefore be independent of that choice. This module proves that independence for the actual KLMC chain. For every coupling \(c\) of the initial position law \(\mu\) and reference law \(\pi\), the sample measure is explicitly \(c\otimes Q\), where \(Q\) supplies the common initial velocity and all phase innovations. The velocity and position components of each innovation stay together, so their correlation is preserved. No convergence or stationary-reference assumption enters these law identities.

steps.title: Build velocity and innovations on each actual product extension
steps.body: The initial coupling has a probability first marginal, hence its joint measure is a probability measure. Its product with the fixed probability source \(Q\) is therefore a probability measure; the local instance records this derived fact. Pull the source velocity \(V\) back through the second projection and take its canonical L² class. Do the same separately for the two components of each supplied phase innovation \(W_n\). Both use the same source point. This gives the pair of L² classes needed by the kinetic analysis without assuming that velocity and position noise are independent. The implementation reuses the existing checked product-noise construction.

steps.title: Identify the chosen L² representatives almost everywhere
steps.body: The canonical Lp representative equals the original pulled-back random variable almost everywhere. For velocity this is the existing product-noise representative theorem. For a phase innovation, intersect the two full-measure sets for its components and apply pair extensionality. Thus the L² pair represents precisely \(W_n(s)\), including all its correlation. This is an almost-everywhere equality of actual random variables, not a comparison of moments or covariances.

steps.title: Define one numerical output law from initialization and fixed source
steps.body: Given a position \(x\) and source point \(s\), start the original pointwise KLMC recursion at \((V(s),x)\), use its phase innovations \(W_n(s)\), and project the final phase state to position. This is productKLMCMap. Its law is the pushforward of \(\mu\otimes Q\), recorded by productKLMCLaw. The definition contains no reference coupling. In particular, it is the same candidate output law for every coupling used to estimate its transport error.

steps.title: Prove the L² numerical chain is exactly the pointwise chain
steps.body: On \(c\otimes Q\), the L² numerical start consists of the pulled-back common velocity and first initial-position coordinate. The reference position's finite second moment together with finite coupling cost supplies a square-integrable first coordinate. Apply the shared L²-to-pointwise KLMC chain theorem. A countable intersection supplies agreement of every phase innovation on one full-measure set; intersect it with the initial velocity and position agreements. Pair extensionality identifies the exact initial phase state, function extensionality identifies the entire innovation sequence, and projection to the position coordinate finishes the equality. Equal initial velocities arise by using the same constructed L² variable; no separate velocity coupling cost is inserted.

steps.title: Derive law independence with almost-everywhere measurable data
steps.body:
The projection \(((x,y),s)\mapsto(x,s)\) sends \(c\otimes Q\) exactly to \(\mu\otimes Q\). Consequently every almost-everywhere measurable function of \((x,s)\) has the same law on both spaces. Lean proves this using the actual projection marginal and the almost-everywhere version of the composition rule for pushforwards. This avoids an unnecessary assumption that arbitrarily selected Lp representatives are everywhere measurable.

The output map is indeed almost-everywhere measurable: the source L² assumptions give that property for velocity and both innovation components. The force is continuous by Lipschitz regularity, so the KLMC update is measurable. Induction propagates measurability through every phase iterate, and projection gives the position output. The final output-law theorem rewrites the L² chain with its proved representative equality, then applies the projection-law identity. Both its initial marginal and its numerical law are derived rather than supplied as fields of a reference interface.

steps.title: Check that the common output has total mass one
steps.body: The independent product of the initial probability law and source law is a probability measure. The preceding almost-everywhere measurability theorem ensures its pushforward remains a probability measure. Lean applies Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map_iff. This establishes an actual numerical output law before any Wasserstein estimate is attached to it. Canonical Gaussian source construction and the stationary continuous reference are additional layers needed for the final unconditional sampler theorem.

KineticLangevin/OBABOContraction.lean.title: The actual nonlinear OBABO map contracts with the source constants
KineticLangevin/OBABOContraction.lean.summary: For a differentiable, m-strongly convex potential with M-Lipschitz gradient, the actual OBABO step driven by common thermostat vectors contracts the modified energy whenever \(\gamma^2\ge4M\) and \(33\gamma^3h\le m\). The thermostat amplitude is arbitrary: it disappears through synchronous cancellation. This proves a property of the implemented map and its actual iterates, rather than postulating a contractive transition.

steps.title: Derive the small-step and exponential damping bounds
steps.body: The source restrictions imply \(\gamma h\le1/132\): multiply by the positive \(\gamma^2\) and use \(33\gamma^3h\le m\le M\le\gamma^2/4\). Squaring gives the weaker estimates \(\gamma h\le1\), \(12\gamma^2h^2\le1\) used by the residual budget. With \(\delta=e^{-\gamma h/2}\), positivity and monotonicity of the exponential give \(0\le\delta\le1\). The global tangent inequality \(e^{-u}\ge1-u\) gives \(1-\delta\le\gamma h/2\) and \(\delta^2-1+\gamma h\ge0\). The proved quadratic exponential bound gives its upper bound \(\gamma^2h^2/2\). These are scalar facts about the exact damping used in the code.

steps.title: Apply the complete remainder estimate to the actual two-kick step
steps.body:
For two states driven by the same noises, set \(x=x_0-y_0\), \(v=v_0-w_0\), \(F_0= abla f(x_0)- abla f(y_0)\), and let \(x_1,y_1\) be the actual drift-stage positions. The average second-kick force is \(S=(F_0+ abla f(x_1)- abla f(y_1))/2\). Its sector error is exactly \(e=M\|(x_1-y_1)-x\|/2\). Lipschitzness bounds \(F_0\), while the actual position update bounds the change in difference by \(h\|v\|+h^2M\|x\|/2\). The centered interpolation inequality for the original potential at both pairs yields the average-force sector estimate and then \(\|S\|\le M\|x\|+e\).

The source-metric drift estimate and all damping bounds now satisfy the preceding module’s explicit algebra theorem. Finally module checks that the exact difference of the two implemented O-B-A-B-O steps equals that algebraic map, including both noisy intermediate positions. The result is \(E(z_+-w_+)\le(1-mh/(3\gamma))E(z-w)\). No Gaussian assumption is needed for this pathwise theorem, because the same additive vectors cancel exactly.

steps.title: Iterate and project to the physical position
steps.body: The small-step restrictions ensure the factor \(q=1-mh/(3\gamma)\) is nonnegative. Induction then applies the actual one-step theorem and multiplies the preceding energy inequality by q, giving \(E(Z_n-W_n)\le q^nE(Z_0-W_0)\) for any two actual recursions with the same two input vectors at every step. When the initial velocities agree, the initial mixed energy is exactly the squared initial position distance. The lower metric equivalence gives \(\|X_n-Y_n\|^2\le2q^n\|X_0-Y_0\|^2\). Both sides are nonnegative, so Lean applies the square comparison and the nonnegative square-root identity to obtain \(\|X_n-Y_n\|\le\sqrt{2q^n}\|X_0-Y_0\|\). This is a direct statement about numerical iterates; identifying an invariant law and quantifying discretization bias are separate analytic steps.

KineticLangevin/KineticSplitting.lean.title: Concrete Verlet–OU splitting and genuine local defects
KineticLangevin/KineticSplitting.lean.summary: The splitting is an explicit numerical map: velocity Verlet for the Hamiltonian drift, then exponential velocity damping and a supplied filtered additive increment. Its stability and local kinetic Euler defect are proved from the map algebra. The filtered increment is written by deterministic integration by parts, matching the canonical Brownian segment identity proved separately.

steps.title: Damp velocity while retaining position
steps.body: The map is \(D_\delta(v,x)=(\delta v,x)\). For \(0\le\delta\le1\), its velocity difference has norm \(\delta\|v-w\|\) and its position difference is unchanged. Each is bounded by the original maximum product norm, hence the full map is nonexpansive. Lean proves the two coordinate bounds and combines them using max_le. This uses the actual usual product norm rather than an undeclared Euclidean phase norm.

steps.title: Construct and stabilize the actual Verlet–OU step
steps.body: The explicit step is \(S_h(z,N)=O_{e^{-\gamma h},N}(V_hz)\). Two synchronously driven steps have exactly the same additive increment, which cancels. Exponential damping lies in \((0,1]\) for nonnegative friction and step, so it is nonexpansive. The already proved Verlet stability bound gives \[\|S_h(z,N)-S_h(w,N)\|\le[1+(M+1)^2h]\|z-w\|\] for \(h\le1\). Lean first checks the exact noise-cancellation identity and then composes these two genuine bounds.

steps.title: Derive exponential damping errors without dividing by friction
steps.body: The response balances \(\gamma\psi_1=1-e^{-\gamma h}\) and \(\gamma\psi_2=h-\psi_1\) imply \(e^{-\gamma h}-1+\gamma h=\gamma^2\psi_2\). Since \(0\le\psi_2\le h^2/2\), the absolute Euler remainder is bounded by \(\gamma^2h^2/2\). Also the exponential tangent inequality gives \(0\le1-e^{-\gamma h}\le\gamma h\). Lean obtains both estimates from exact identities and checks all sign conditions. The formulas remain valid at zero friction.

steps.title: Compare the damped Hamiltonian Euler stage with full kinetic Euler
steps.body: Damp the Hamiltonian Euler stage and subtract full kinetic Euler. Their position components agree exactly, while their velocity difference is \((e^{-\gamma h}-1+\gamma h)v+(1-e^{-\gamma h})h\,g(x)\). The preceding scalar estimates bound this by a quadratic expression. Lipschitz force growth \(\|g(x)\|\le M\|z\|+\|g(0)\|\) yields the displayed \(h^2[\gamma^2/2+\gamma(M+1)](\|z\|+\|g(0)\|)\) bound. Lean proves the exact vector identity, bounds its two terms, and combines nonnegative scalar factors.

steps.title: Bound the complete deterministic kinetic Euler defect
steps.body: Insert the damped Hamiltonian Euler stage between the actual split step and full kinetic Euler. Nonexpansiveness of damping preserves the proved Verlet-versus-Hamiltonian-Euler defect. Add the damped-stage defect just established. The noise increment is retained exactly on both sides and cancels, giving \[\|S_h(z,N)-[z-hd(z)+(N,0)]\|\le h^2C(\|z\|+\|g(0)\|),\quad C=(M+1)(M+2)+\gamma^2/2+\gamma(M+1).\] Lean applies the triangle inequality through this explicit intermediate state and normalizes the coefficient algebra.

steps.title: Use the actual filtered additive increment
steps.body: For a continuous additive velocity input \(B\), define \[N_{a,h}=B_{a+h}-B_a-\gamma\int_0^h e^{-\gamma(h-s)}(B_{a+s}-B_a)\,ds.\] This is the deterministic integration-by-parts representation of the exact OU response. If the input oscillation over the interval is at most \(\eta\), exponential damping is at most one, so \(\|N_{a,h}-(B_{a+h}-B_a)\|\le\gamma h\eta\). Lean subtracts the matching increment exactly, moves the scalar outside the norm, and bounds the actual integral by its interval length and pointwise integrand bound. The Brownian segment module independently proves precisely this identity for the constructed Gaussian source.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalVectorSegments..title: The canonical vector Brownian innovations and initial Gaussian velocity
KineticLangevin/CanonicalVectorSegments..summary: The paper draws correlated velocity and position innovations in each spatial coordinate, independently across coordinates and time steps. Here every such draw is realized from the existing product of scalar canonical Brownian sources. The entire constructed array is proved to have exactly the previously defined Gaussian product law; equality of a few moments alone is not used as a substitute for equality of laws.

steps.title: Transport independence along an actual law
steps.body: A measurable map \(Y\) with actual law \(Q\) can pull back any independent measurable family defined on \(Q\). Lean proves this by the characterization of mutual independence through equality with the infinite product of marginal laws. It applies the pushforward composition theorem to the joint family and to each marginal. This elementary tool is used repeatedly to transfer established independence to the concrete Brownian source.

steps.title: Build correlated scalar and spatial blocks
steps.body: A scalar block consists of all deterministic response kernels applied to the same Brownian interval. Packing their values with WithLp.toLp gives a finite Euclidean vector whose law is the Gram Gaussian already proved in BrownianSegments. A vector block evaluates that scalar block on each spatial coordinate source. Every map is measurable because each L² representative is strongly measurable, coordinate evaluation is measurable, and finite or infinite coordinatewise packing preserves measurability.

steps.title: Prove the law of the entire array
steps.body: For one spatial source, disjoint Brownian intervals give independent scalar blocks. Different spatial sources are independent by the explicit product construction. The theorem iIndepFun_uncurry' combines these two facts into independence over iteration-coordinate pairs; reindexing swaps their order. Each marginal has the established Gram-Gaussian law, so hasLaw_infinitePi identifies the full array distribution. Currying the array is a measurable equivalence, and the product-measure curry theorem identifies the distribution as an independent stream of complete spatial blocks. Pullback along this actual path law proves independence across time steps.

steps.title: Identify the existing KLMC Gaussian stream exactly
steps.body: For \(d\) finite spatial coordinates, the pair-indexed array has exactly the existing kernelNoisePath law. Specializing the response family to \((\psi_0,\psi_1)\) and packing each response into a vector produces the actual unscaled velocity-position innovation. Composition of the stream law with the existing klmcInnovation map proves its exact distribution. Independence of the full vector blocks survives this measurable packing. Each vector coordinate lies in L² by the Brownian isometry; pulling it back along spatial evaluation and using MemLp.of_eval_piLp proves both phase components have finite second moments.

steps.title: Adjoin the independent initial Gaussian velocity
steps.body:
The source for a sampler is \(Q=\mathcal N(0,I_d)\otimes P_{\mathrm{Brownian}}\). Its first projection is the actual standard Gaussian initial velocity. Its second projection carries all constructed innovations. Product-measure projection laws prove the velocity law and preserve the innovation law. The product independence theorem proves that initial velocity is independent of the entire future innovation stream, while measure-preserving pullback gives all required L² bounds. An arbitrary initial-position coupling can subsequently be extended by this same fixed source, independently of that coupling.

Pullback along the second projection also proves mutual independence of complete innovations across all iterations on this enlarged source; the new Gaussian velocity does not alter the noise law.

KineticLangevin/VectorSegmentEquations.l.title: Continuous vector Brownian responses in L²
KineticLangevin/VectorSegmentEquations.l.summary: The scalar Brownian equations must also hold for Euclidean random vectors so they can drive the actual L² kinetic diffusion used by the contraction proof. A continuous linear spatial assembly map achieves this directly: it preserves sums, scalar multiples, continuity, and Bochner time integrals.

steps.title: Assemble scalar L² variables through a continuous linear map
steps.body: For a scalar random variable \(Z\), spatial assembly produces the vector \((Z(\omega_i))_i\), evaluating it on independent spatial copies of the canonical source. The Lean definition is a finite sum. Each summand first pulls back along a measure-preserving coordinate evaluation, then inserts the scalar into one Euclidean basis coordinate. Both operations are continuous linear maps on L². The representative theorem is proved by the finite-sum almost-everywhere identity and the explicit representatives of these two maps; Euclidean extensionality verifies each coordinate. This construction avoids interchanging pointwise evaluation with an L² Bochner integral.

steps.title: Define vector responses and prove continuity
steps.body: The vector response is the spatial assembly of the actual scalar response on \((a,a+t]\). The vector Brownian input is the assembly of the scalar Brownian increment. Their definitions remain on the existing canonical product source. The response representative theorem gives exactly the expected independent-coordinate vector. Continuity in time follows by composing the continuous scalar response with the continuous linear assembly map.

steps.title: Lift the exact primitive and damped integral equations
steps.body: The position response satisfies \(P^a_t=\int_0^tV^a_sds\), and the velocity response satisfies \(V^a_t=W^a_t-\gamma\int_0^tV^a_sds\). These equalities follow from the already proved scalar equations by applying the spatial assembly map. The proof commutes that continuous linear map with each Bochner integral using intervalIntegral_comp_comm. Thus the exact filtered Brownian input required by the generic mild-equation theorem is constructed for the vector L² diffusion.

steps.title: Identify the input with canonical vector Brownian increments
steps.body: The lifted input is proved almost everywhere equal to the vector whose coordinates are \(B_i(a+t)-B_i(a)\) for the existing canonical coordinate process. The scalar subtraction identity is pulled back through each measure-preserving spatial projection and combined with the spatial representative theorem. Continuity follows by identifying the increment with the unit-kernel vector response. This connects the L² forcing to the actual canonical vector Brownian construction.

steps.title: Identify the OU increment and numerical innovation endpoints
steps.body: The vector velocity response is exactly \(V^a_t=W^a_t-\gamma\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}W^a_sds\). Lean applies spatial assembly to the established scalar integration-by-parts formula, uses its linearity, and commutes it with the continuous Bochner integrand. This is precisely the OU input increment used by the kinetic splitting limit. At each grid interval, the paired L² velocity and position response endpoints are proved almost everywhere equal to the pointwise canonicalKLMCInnovation already equipped with the exact Gaussian law. The endpoint proof combines the two actual representative equalities with Prod.ext; it does not replace the constructed inputs by new independent Gaussian variables.

KineticLangevin/KineticSplittingConverge.title: The actual Verlet–OU chain converges to the kinetic integral solution
KineticLangevin/KineticSplittingConverge.summary: This module proves the missing numerical limit directly in a Banach space, including the intended space of square-integrable random variables. The actual scheme uses explicit Verlet stages, exact exponential damping, and the filtered increments of the same continuous additive input as the actual kinetic equation. Compact continuity supplies every local modulus used in the proof. No stationary solution, local-error contract, or numerical-convergence hypothesis is assumed.

steps.title: Construct the splitting on the actual grid input
steps.body: Starting from \(X_0=z_0\), the next state is \(X_{k+1}=S_h(X_k,N_{kh,h})\), where \(S_h\) is the explicit Verlet–OU step and \(N_{a,h}\) is the actual filtered increment of the supplied continuous input \(B\). Lean defines this recursion directly. Each stage uses the correct grid time \(kh\); the forcing is not replaced by an unrelated Gaussian with the same marginal variance.

steps.title: Compare one numerical increment with the exact kinetic path
steps.body:
Let the actual path satisfy \(Y_t-z_0=-\int_0^t d(Y_s)\,ds+(B_t,0)\), where \(d(v,x)=(\gamma v+g(x),-v)\). Subtract its equations at \(a\) and \(a+h\). Freezing its drift gives an exact Euler identity with remainder \(D_{a,h}=\int_0^h[d(Y_{a+s})-d(Y_a)]\,ds\). A drift oscillation bound \(\eta\) gives \(\|D_{a,h}\|\le h\eta\). The matching OU input differs from \(B_{a+h}-B_a\) by at most \(\gamma h\eta\) when the input oscillation is also at most \(\eta\). Finally, the proved explicit splitting defect contributes at most \(h^2C(R+\|g(0)\|)\), where \(\|Y_t\|\le R\) and \(C=(M+1)(M+2)+\gamma^2/2+\gamma(M+1)\). Lean constructs the grid and interval-membership facts, derives the exact increment equation through adjacent-interval integration, proves the local-defect identity, and bounds each of these three genuine terms.

For \(e_k=\|X_k-Y_{kh}\|\), synchronous numerical stability then gives \[e_{k+1}\le[1+(M+1)^2h]e_k+h\{hC(R+\|g(0)\|)+(1+\gamma)\eta\}.\] The actual initial equation and \(B_0=0\) prove \(e_0=0\). The checked finite recurrence estimate and \((1+ah)^n\le e^{aT}\), with \(nh=T\), yield the displayed finite-horizon bound. Every modulus premise belongs to this intermediate estimate and is derived from continuity in the next theorem.

steps.title: Derive all moduli and prove convergence
steps.body: The continuous exact path is bounded on \([0,T]\). Its drift path is continuous by global Lipschitz continuity of \(g\), and the additive input \(B\) is continuous. Compactness makes both uniformly continuous. Given any target error \(\varepsilon>0\), choose a common oscillation tolerance \(\eta=\varepsilon/(D+1)\), where the explicit finite horizon constant \(D\) contains the state bound, the splitting defect coefficient, friction, and the stability exponential. Since \(h_n=T/(n+1)\to0\), the mesh is eventually at most one, at most \(\eta\), and below both continuity radii. The finite error estimate is then at most \(\eta D<\varepsilon\). Lean obtains the two compact uniform-continuity radii, combines the four eventual mesh bounds, instantiates the actual finite estimate, and checks this final scalar comparison. Thus the concrete scheme converges to every actual continuous kinetic integral solution driven by the same input.

steps.title: Identify the limit with the constructed kinetic flow
steps.body: The earlier Picard construction supplies a continuous solution for every initial state and every compact continuous forcing path, with its actual kinetic integral identity already proved. Its normalized forcing is globally continuous and vanishes at zero. Substituting these checked facts into the generic Banach convergence theorem proves that the splitting limit is exactly kineticFlow at the requested horizon. This ties the approximation to the existing jointly continuous solution map, not to an unspecified solution chosen by a new contract.

KineticLangevin/OBABOLaw.lean.title: Actual independent-noise OBABO laws contract in Wasserstein distance
KineticLangevin/OBABOLaw.lean.summary: The preceding pathwise energy contraction now becomes a theorem about the actual Markov laws. An explicit invertible change of coordinates turns the modified energy into Euclidean squared distance. Measurability, the commuting law identity, independent source extension, and passage to the Wasserstein infimum are all proved. The result holds for every probability law of the two thermostat inputs, including the independent Gaussian law used by the sampler.

steps.title: Build and verify the weighted-coordinate inverse
steps.body: The weighted Hilbert coordinates are \(T(v,x)=(x+bv,c v)\), where \(c=\sqrt{a-b^2}\). For \(b^2<a\), the inverse is \(T^{-1}(u,w)=(w/c,u-bw/c)\). Lean first proves \(c\ne0\), then uses the inverse cancellation identities for real scalars to check both compositions. The transform commutes with subtraction by direct module algebra. Its continuity follows from continuity of scalar multiplication, coordinate projections, addition, and the Euclidean-product identification. The local measurable structure on WithLp 2 is explicitly its Borel structure, so these continuous maps supply the measurable changes of variables required for the measure arguments.

steps.title: Conjugate the actual noisy step and prove its Lipschitz bound
steps.body: Define the transformed update by the actual conjugation \(\widetilde P_\xi=T\circ P_\xi\circ T^{-1}\), retaining the original two noise arguments and their damping and amplitude. Continuity is a composition of the verified inverse, the actual O-B-A-B-O formulas, and the verified transform. The condition \(\gamma^2\ge4M>0\) makes \(b^2<a\). Apply the actual nonlinear energy contraction to \(T^{-1}y,T^{-1}z\); replace each energy by the square of its transformed norm and use the two inverse identities. The nonnegative square comparison yields \(\|\widetilde P_\xi y-\widetilde P_\xi z\|\le\sqrt{1-mh/(3\gamma)}\|y-z\|\). Every geometric fact needed for this estimate is derived explicitly.

steps.title: Prove that Markov iteration commutes with the coordinate change
steps.body: obaboLaws is the repeated independent-noise product-and-pushforward transition of the original implemented step; weightedObaboLaws uses its transformed implementation. A generic induction proves the commuting diagram for any measurable maps satisfying \(T(F(x,\xi))=G(Tx,\xi)\). At each step, Measure.map_prod_map proves that transforming the current state commutes with adjoining an independent innovation. Two applications of Measure.map_map reduce the law identity to the actual pointwise conjugacy. Instantiating with the verified inverse gives \(T_\#\mathcal L_n(\mu)=\widetilde{\mathcal L}_n(T_\#\mu)\), so the contracting measures are the genuine transformed sampler laws.

steps.title: Take the true coupling infimum and iterate the actual laws
steps.body: Let \(r=\sqrt{1-mh/(3\gamma)}\). For every coupling of two current laws, append one common innovation independently. Its two output marginals are the actual Markov outputs, and the pointwise bound gives output transport cost at most r times the input coupling cost. The previously proved random-map theorem takes the infimum over all input couplings; it assumes no optimal coupling exists. Induction, with probability of each actual iterated law proved internally, yields \(W_2(\widetilde{\mathcal L}_n\mu,\widetilde{\mathcal L}_n\nu)\le r^nW_2(\mu,\nu)\). The commuting law identity transfers this to the original laws measured in the modified geometry. The extended-real theorem is unconditional on transport finiteness. If the initial weighted transport distance is finite, the proved upper bound first establishes finiteness of the output and then permits conversion to the real-valued Wasserstein estimate. Stationarity and numerical target bias are separate claims, not hidden inputs to this law contraction.

KineticLangevin/GibbsTarget.lean.title: The actual Gaussian-times-Gibbs phase target
KineticLangevin/GibbsTarget.lean.summary: The normalized kinetic target is the independent product of a standard Gaussian velocity and the intended Gibbs position measure. This module identifies that product with an explicit scalar normalization of the actual Hamiltonian weighted measure, transfers the proved Hamiltonian invariance, and proves exact Gaussian thermostat invariance on the correct independent-noise product. Its position and velocity marginals are exact pushforward identities. These two invariant substeps are ingredients for kinetic Gibbs stationarity; passage to the continuous kinetic limit is a separate theorem.

steps.title: Identify the Gaussian thermal density by its actual law
steps.body: The already checked Gaussian proposal density at step \(h=1/2\) and center zero is exactly the standard Gaussian. Its scalar precision is \(1/(4h)=1/2\), and its affine map is the identity. Consequently its density is \(c_Ge^{-\|v\|^2/2}\), where \(c_G\) is the inverse of the actual finite Gaussian integral. Lean first normalizes the precision and the identity pushforward, then factors the positive normalizer out of the density using withDensity_smul and ENNReal.ofReal_mul. The remaining real exponential identity follows by scalar algebra. This is an equality with the existing probability measure stdGaussian, not an informal naming of a radial weight.

steps.title: Normalize the Hamiltonian weighted measure explicitly
steps.body:
Define \(\Pi=\varphi\otimes\pi\), velocity first, with \(\varphi\) the actual standard Gaussian and \(\pi\) the normalized Gibbs measure of \(f\). The Gaussian density identity and the existing definition of \(\pi\) give

\[\Pi=(c_G/Z_f)\,e^{-f(x)-\|v\|^2/2}\,dv\,dx.\]

Lean distributes the two scalar normalizers through the product of measures, then rewrites the previously proved factorization of the Hamiltonian Gibbs weight. Strong convexity with \(m>0\) makes the position normalization positive and finite, so the product is a probability measure. Its probability proof invokes the already derived Gibbs probability theorem; normalization is not an assumption about a stationary process.

steps.title: Transfer the proved Hamiltonian invariance to the canonical target
steps.body: The actual selected Hamiltonian flow already preserves the unnormalized Hamiltonian weighted measure, by the corrected-Verlet approximation and its proved numerical limit. Multiplying a measure by a fixed scalar commutes with a measurable pushforward. The explicit normalization identity therefore gives \((H_t)_\#\Pi=\Pi\). Lean supplies measurability from continuous dependence of the endpoint on its initial phase state, uses Measure.map_smul, and applies the proved Hamiltonian invariance theorem. This statement has only the potential assumptions and finite-dimensional setting; no invariant-target hypothesis remains.

steps.title: Prove the thermostat identity with fresh independent Gaussian noise
steps.body:
Let \(X\) have any probability position law, independently of a standard Gaussian velocity \(V\), and let \(\xi\) be a fresh independent standard Gaussian. If \(a^2+b^2=1\), then \((aV+b\xi,X)\) again has the original independent velocity-position law. The input is explicitly \((\varphi\otimes\pi_X)\otimes\varphi\). A measure-preserving reassociation and swap reorder its three coordinates to \((V,\xi),X\). The previously proved Gaussian linear-combination law acts on the first pair; the position coordinate is unchanged. Lean verifies both the coordinate permutation and its product-measure pushforward before applying Measure.map_prod_map. Thus independence and the output marginal are derived, not supplied.

Specializing the arbitrary position law to the actual normalized Gibbs target proves thermostat invariance of \(\Pi\). Exact OU evolution chooses \(a=e^{-\gamma h}\) and \(b=\sqrt{1-e^{-2\gamma h}}\); an OBABO half-step uses the corresponding half-interval coefficients. The theorem admits both choices through the explicit variance balance.

steps.title: Recover the two equilibrium marginals exactly
steps.body: Projecting the independent product \(\varphi\otimes\pi\) to position integrates out a unit-mass Gaussian and leaves \(\pi\). Projecting to velocity integrates out the normalized position measure and leaves \(\varphi\). Lean installs the derived Gibbs probability instance and applies the two product-projection identities, simplifying their unit total-mass factors. These equalities supply the target position marginal and Gaussian velocity marginal used by the later L² coupling theorem once stationarity of the full kinetic dynamics is proved.

KineticLangevin/KineticSplittingLp.lean.title: The L² splitting is the actual vector algorithm almost everywhere
KineticLangevin/KineticSplittingLp.lean.summary: The deterministic convergence theorem applies to a Banach space of square-integrable random variables. To connect that analysis to the intended stochastic method, this module checks every elementary stage on actual representatives. The lifted force is the original force almost everywhere, and the supplied noise is retained unchanged. Induction then identifies the entire L² recursion with the vector recursion.

steps.title: Expose the chain driven by explicit filtered innovations
steps.body: The innovation chain starts at its supplied phase state and recursively applies the explicit Verlet–OU step with innovation \(N_k\). The earlier continuous-input chain is exactly this chain with \(N_k=N_{kh,h}(B)\). Lean proves this equality by induction, unfolding the two actual recursions at the successor step. This representation lets the probability layer identify the innovation array law independently of the deterministic input analysis.

steps.title: Check force kicks on actual L² representatives
steps.body: The lifted force \(G\) is constructed from the actual Lipschitz force \(g\), and the shared lifting theorem gives \(G(X)(\omega)=g(X(\omega))\) almost everywhere. The representative identities for subtraction and scalar multiplication therefore give \([V-hG(X)](\omega)=V(\omega)-hg(X(\omega))\). Position is unchanged. Lean intersects the three almost-everywhere events and proves equality of the two phase coordinates. No new vector-field or output-law assumption is introduced.

steps.title: Check free transport and the full supplied thermostat noise
steps.body: The representative of \(X+hV\) is \(X(\omega)+hV(\omega)\), proving the free drift identity. Likewise the representative of \(\delta V+\sigma\Xi\) is \(\delta V(\omega)+\sigma\Xi(\omega)\), proving the OU stage identity. Lean explicitly intersects the addition and scalar-multiplication representative events and retains the exact supplied innovation \(\Xi\). These are pathwise stage identities and do not presume any Gaussian distribution.

steps.title: Compose the checked stages into the actual Verlet–OU map
steps.body: The Verlet step is the kick–drift–kick composition. Apply the checked representative identity at each actual intermediate L² state, intersect the resulting almost-everywhere events, and substitute them in order. The complete splitting then composes this checked Verlet map with the checked OU stage, using exactly the damping \(e^{-\gamma h}\) and supplied filtered innovation. Lean performs these successive substitutions, so the state at which the second force is evaluated remains the updated position.

steps.title: Identify every numerical iterate with the original vector chain
steps.body: The initial phase representatives agree by definition. Assuming agreement at step \(n\), the checked full-step identity and the induction hypothesis give agreement at step \(n+1\), driven by the same innovation representative \(N_n(\omega)\). Lean intersects these two almost-everywhere events and rewrites the recursive definitions. Hence every L² iterate analyzed by the convergence theorem is the actual vector splitting algorithm on the same probability source.

KineticLangevin/CoupledSegments.lean.title: Constructing the actual reference and auxiliary coupling segments
KineticLangevin/CoupledSegments.lean.summary: The local KLMC analysis compares a numerical state with an exact reference state. On each step it inserts an auxiliary exact path started at the numerical state and driven by precisely the same additive input as the reference. This module constructs those paths from the proved kinetic flow. The differential, kinematic and mild identities used in the local-error theorem follow from their actual integral equations.

steps.title: Restart an actual integral solution at any time
steps.body: If \(Y_t-Y_0=-\int_0^tg(Y_s)ds+W_t\), then \(Y_{a+t}-Y_a=-\int_0^tg(Y_{a+s})ds+(W_{a+t}-W_a)\) whenever the shifted interval lies in the original horizon. Lean subtracts the two actual equations at \(a+t\) and \(a\), splits the continuous drift integral at \(a\), and changes variables in the remaining integral. Additive group algebra cancels the shared starting point. This supplies the exact time-shift identity required when segmenting a continuous diffusion.

steps.title: Use a raw continuous input with the selected kinetic flow
steps.body: A continuous input \(W\) is restricted to the compact solution horizon, producing the existing VelocityForcing object. If \(W_0=0\), the flow's normalized clipped extension equals \(W_t\) at every time in that horizon. Lean uses the exact projection identity projIcc_of_mem to prove this. The selected segment is then the existing Picard-constructed kineticFlow with that compact input. Its specification gives continuity, its true initial condition, and the exact integral equation with the original raw input.

steps.title: Derive velocity, kinematic and mild equations by projection
steps.body: Applying the velocity continuous linear projection to the kinetic integral equation gives \(V_t-V_0=-\int_0^t(\gamma V_s+u g(X_s))ds+W_t\). Applying the position projection gives \(X_t-X_0=\int_0^tV_sds\), because the positional input is exactly zero. In both cases Lean commutes the projection with the Bochner integral. If the actual filtered input satisfies \(B_t=W_t-\gamma\int_0^tB_sds\), the proved Banach-space integrating-factor theorem gives \(V_T=\psi_0(T)V_0-\int_0^Te^{-\gamma(T-s)}u g(X_s)ds+B_T\). Thus the exponential mild equation is a consequence of the kinetic equation, rather than a new stochastic hypothesis.

steps.title: Construct exact reference segments and the implemented numerical chain
steps.body: The reference chain starts from its supplied actual phase vector. At each iteration, its next state is the endpoint of the selected exact kinetic segment driven by that iteration's input. The corresponding reference segment is the same selected path, so its endpoint matches the next reference state by definition. The numerical chain instead performs the actual frozen-force exponential update with innovation \((B_n(h),\int_0^hB_n(s)ds)\). This uses the constructed filtered input and its genuine positional primitive.

steps.title: Construct the auxiliary exact path from the current numerical state
steps.body: The auxiliary segment is an actual selected exact kinetic solution whose initial condition is the current exponential-integrator state. It receives exactly the same raw Brownian input as the reference segment on that iteration. The two specification theorems prove continuity, exact starting values, reference endpoint matching, and their shared-input integral equations. Every field comes from the kinetic flow construction; no contraction or local-error inequality is inserted into the definitions.

steps.title: Discharge the local-error proof's kinematic and mild requirements
steps.body: The constructed auxiliary path has its positional primitive identity by the general kinetic projection theorem. Its exponentially weighted force formula follows by restricting its actual integral equation to any smaller time \(t\le h\), restricting the filtered-input balance to the same interval, and applying the generic mild theorem. Lean explicitly checks the interval inclusions and simplifies the inverse mass \(u=1\). The remaining stochastic work concerns the law and stationarity of the reference; the coupling segments and their analytic identities are concrete constructions.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalSplitting.lean.title: Splitting convergence on the actual constructed vector Brownian source
KineticLangevin/CanonicalSplitting.lean.summary: The deterministic input in the splitting theorem is now identified with the actual canonical vector Brownian motion in L². Its filtered increments are exactly the constructed Gaussian segment convolutions, including the fluctuation-dissipation scaling. Consequently the innovation-driven numerical chain and the continuous-input chain coincide on the same source, and the actual L² chain converges to its kinetic integral solution.

steps.title: Keep scaling and source lifts exact
steps.body: The OU input construction is linear in the additive input. Multiplying \(B\) by a real coefficient \(c\) multiplies both its matching increment and its exponential convolution by \(c\). More generally, a continuous linear map \(L\) commutes with this construction: it commutes with subtraction, scalar multiplication, and the Bochner interval integral of the continuous integrand. Lean proves these exact identities by integral linearity and continuous-linear integral commutation. The latter applies, in particular, to measure-preserving pullbacks that extend the Brownian source by an independent initial state.

steps.title: Construct the actual continuous L² Brownian input
steps.body: The input is the already constructed vector Brownian increment from time zero, evaluated at \(t_+=\max\{t,0\}\). This supplies a globally defined real-time function, anchored at zero. The proved continuity of vector Brownian increments in L² and continuity of \(t\mapsto t_+\) prove continuity of this input. At zero the underlying increment is the difference of a Brownian value with itself, so it is exactly zero. Lean unfolds the actual source definitions to check this anchor.

steps.title: Identify actual input increments and OU segment responses
steps.body: The difference between the anchored values at \(a+t\) and \(a\) cancels their common time-zero value, leaving the actual canonical Brownian increment on \((a,a+t]\). The independently proved segment convolution identity gives \[Z_{a,t}=\Delta B_{a,t}-\gamma\int_0^t e^{-\gamma(t-s)}\Delta B_{a,s}\,ds.\] This is exactly the deterministic ouInputIncrement used in the splitting theorem. Lean rewrites the endpoint increment, compares the actual interval integrands, and uses nonnegativity of the integration time to remove its real-to-nonnegative-time clamp. Scaling by any \(c\), including \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\), follows from the checked linearity identity. The equality is of actual L² variables, stronger than merely matching marginal Gaussian laws.

steps.title: Identify the entire canonical innovation chain
steps.body: On a mesh of nonnegative size \(h\), the continuous-input chain uses the increment \(N_{kh,h}\). The preceding actual identity replaces this by \(cZ_{kh,h}\) for every grid index. The explicit-innovation recursion therefore agrees exactly with the continuous-input recursion. Lean first uses the proved equality between the two chain representations and then substitutes the actual OU increment identity at each nonnegative grid time.

steps.title: Conclude actual L² convergence on the canonical source
steps.body: Apply the generic Banach splitting theorem to the continuous canonical input \(cB\), its proved zero initial value, and the actual continuous kinetic integral solution \(Y\) driven by that same input. Rewrite the resulting continuous-input chain by the proved canonical innovation-chain identity. This yields convergence of the explicit chain with actual Gaussian convolution innovations on the mesh \(T/(n+1)\) to \(Y_T\). Lean checks the nonnegative-time casts in the mesh and grid endpoints. The integral-solution premise is the actual equation constructed elsewhere by Picard existence; no stationarity or numerical convergence is supplied as a contract.

KineticLangevin/VerletLocal.lean.title: A genuine local state comparison with exact Hamiltonian dynamics
KineticLangevin/VerletLocal.lean.summary: To quantify sampling bias, compare the implemented O–Verlet–O step with a reference that uses exact Hamiltonian motion between the same two thermostat updates. Exact Hamiltonian motion and the thermostat preserve the Gibbs target separately. This module derives the actual local state error from the Hamiltonian integral equations. It works in any real Hilbert space, including L², where uniform velocity and force norm bounds are second-moment statements.

steps.title: Integrate the Hamiltonian equations instead of assuming a local error
steps.body: The Hamiltonian equations are \(v(t)-v(0)=-\int_0^t g(x(s))ds\) and \(x(t)-x(0)=\int_0^t v(s)ds\). If the force norm is at most G, the integral norm inequality gives \(\|v(t)-v(0)\|\le Gt\). Subtract \(tv(0)\) from the position equation; the result is the integral of the velocity increment. Integrating the derived envelope \(Gs\) gives the actual Euler-position defect \(\|x(t)-x(0)-tv(0)\|\le Gt^2/2\). Lean proves the exact integral identities using integrability from continuity before applying either inequality.

steps.title: Compare both Verlet components to the true endpoint
steps.body: The implemented drift-stage position is \(x_V=x_0+hv_0-h^2g(x_0)/2\). Its difference from the Euler position has norm at most \(Gh^2/2\); adding the exact position defect proves \(\|x_V-x(h)\|\le Gh^2\). For velocity, subtract the frozen-force Euler value \(v_0-hg(x_0)\) from both trajectories. The exact difference is the integral of \(g(x(s))-g(x_0)\), bounded by \(MC h^2/2\) using Lipschitzness and the actual kinematics with velocity norm C. The Verlet difference is exactly \(-h(g(x_V)-g(x_0))/2\), whose norm is at most \(Mh^2C/2+MGh^3/4\). Combining the two gives \(\|v_V-v(h)\|\le MC h^2+MGh^3/4\). Every residual is computed from the update and the exact path; none is supplied as an opaque accuracy assumption.

steps.title: Express the state defect in the contracting OBABO metric
steps.body:
The upper metric equivalence and completing-square Hilbert representation imply the convenient component estimate \(\|(v,x)\|_E\le2(\|x\|+\|v\|/\sqrt M)\). The proof squares both nonnegative sides, expands the scalar square, and uses \(\sqrt M^2=M\). Inserting the two genuine component defects yields

\[\|\mathrm{Verlet}_h(v_0,x_0)-(v(h),x(h))\|_E\le2h^2\bigl(G+\sqrt M C+\sqrt M G h/4\bigr).\]

This estimate uses only a Lipschitz force and the explicit moment envelopes; no Hessian regularity is required.

steps.title: Couple the implemented OBABO step with the exact target-preserving split
steps.body: Start the Hamiltonian path at the actual first Ornstein–Uhlenbeck half-step. Apply the same final thermostat vector to its endpoint and to the Verlet endpoint. The final additive noise cancels exactly, while the velocity defect is multiplied by \(\delta\). Since \(|\delta|\le1\), its norm is no larger than the Verlet velocity defect, and the position defect is unchanged. Applying the component metric bound therefore gives the same explicit local estimate for the actual O–Verlet–O and O–exact-Hamiltonian–O outputs. In L², an invariant Gibbs Hamiltonian reference supplies \(C=\sqrt d\) and \(G\le\sqrt{Md}\) from the Gaussian velocity marginal and Gibbs score moment theorem. The local bound itself keeps the exact path equations and norm envelopes visible so the probabilistic reference construction must discharge them.

KineticLangevin/MarkovTests.lean.title: Bounded tests of the actual independent-noise Markov chain
KineticLangevin/MarkovTests.lean.summary: To prove that a continuous dynamics preserves its Gibbs distribution, approximate it by concrete random steps. A small one-step weak error at the Gibbs measure must be propagated through those actual steps. The dual transition integrates the next test value against the independent fresh noise. Its measurability, uniform bound and exact relation to the forward law are proved here.

steps.title: Integrate the next test against the fresh noise
steps.body: For a measurable step map \(S(x,\xi)\) and noise probability \(Q\), define \(PF(x)=\int F(S(x,\xi))Q(d\xi)\). The measurable parameter-integral theorem proves that \(PF\) is measurable. If \(\lVert F\rVert\le C\) everywhere, the norm-of-integral inequality gives \(\lVert PF(x)\rVert\le\int C\,dQ=C\). Independence is encoded by the product measure used by the actual Markov update.

steps.title: Prove the duality identity for the implemented recursion
steps.body: The law update is the pushforward of \(\mu\otimes Q\) by \(S\). The pushforward integration formula and Fubini give \(\int F\,d(\mu P)=\int PF\,d\mu\). Boundedness on a probability space supplies integrability. Induction proves that every \(P^nF\) remains measurable and bounded by the original \(C\), and that \(\int F\,d(\mu P^n)=\int P^nF\,d\mu\). Thus the dual operator describes the actual law recursion rather than an assumed sequence of measures.

steps.title: Accumulate one-step weak errors without losing the test bound
steps.body: Suppose every measurable test bounded by \(C\) has one-step defect at \(\pi\) at most \(\delta\). Apply this estimate to \(P^nF\), whose bound is still \(C\). Insert and subtract \(\int P^nF\,d\pi\), apply the triangle inequality, and use the induction hypothesis. The resulting estimate is \(\left|\int F\,d(\pi P^n)-\int F\,d\pi\right|\le n\delta\). No exact invariance is assumed. In the splitting application the rejection bound is quadratic in the time step, so \(n\delta\to0\) on a fixed time interval.

KineticLangevin/LpPhaseLaw.lean.title: Actual phase laws and their L² limits
KineticLangevin/LpPhaseLaw.lean.summary: The phase variable is a pair of actual L² classes, and its law is the pushforward of their measurable representatives. Dual characteristic functions depend continuously on this pair. This identifies a limiting stationary phase law from bounded-test estimates without incorrectly treating the usual maximum product norm as a Hilbert norm.

steps.title: Verify measurability of actual phase representatives
steps.body: Each L² class has a fixed strongly measurable representative. Taking the pair of its velocity and position representatives gives a measurable phase map. Lean uses the two strong-measurability results and the measurable product constructor, making the subsequent pushforward an actual measure.

steps.title: Reduce phase characteristic functions to one real L² variable
steps.body: For a continuous real linear functional \(L\) on phase space, let \(L_v(v)=L(v,0)\) and \(L_x(x)=L(0,x)\). The real L² variable \(R=L_v(V)+L_x(X)\) represents \(L(V(\omega),X(\omega))\) almost everywhere. Its law therefore has scalar characteristic function at frequency one equal to the dual characteristic function of the phase law. The map \((V,X)\mapsto R\) is continuous, since the two continuous linear maps lift continuously to L² and addition is continuous. The existing scalar characteristic-function continuity theorem proves the desired phase continuity. Lean explicitly intersects the representative events for both lifted linear maps and their sum, proves the coordinate decomposition by linearity, rewrites the actual pushforward through \(L\), and composes the two continuous maps.

steps.title: Identify the law of an actual L² limit from vanishing weak errors
steps.body: Suppose actual phase pairs \(S_n\) converge in the product of L² spaces to \(S\), and their bounded complex-test errors relative to a fixed finite measure \(\pi\) are eventually bounded by \(\delta_n\to0\). For each dual functional use the norm-one test \(F(z)=e^{iLz}\). The error squeeze gives convergence of the approximating characteristic functions to that of \(\pi\); the continuity theorem gives convergence of the same sequence to the characteristic function of the actual limiting phase law. Uniqueness of limits equates them, and uniqueness of finite measures from their dual characteristic functions gives \(P\circ S^{-1}=\pi\). Lean rewrites the actual phase expectation by the measurable pushforward formula and invokes the checked scalar squeeze and measure-uniqueness theorems. The weak estimates must be proved by the concrete numerical and probability layers; stationary output is not assumed.

KineticLangevin/SegmentGlobal.lean.title: Stitched exact segments are the actual global kinetic solution
KineticLangevin/SegmentGlobal.lean.summary: A reference defined one interval at a time must be identified with the actual continuous kinetic process whose stationarity is proved separately. The bridge here uses the true shifted-input equation and uniqueness. It does not assume a Markov transition formula or independence of arbitrarily chosen reference segments.

steps.title: Identify a selected local solution with a shifted global path
steps.body: Start with an actual continuous global solution \(Y\), and suppose the local input is the actual increment \(W_t=B_{a+t}-B_a\). The previously proved time-shift lemma shows \(Y_{a+t}\) satisfies the same kinetic integral equation on the local horizon. The selected local solution starts at \(Y_a\). Lean checks the two initial conditions, the shared additive input, and continuity, then invokes the proved uniqueness theorem for the globally Lipschitz kinetic drift. Their equality follows at every time in the local interval.

steps.title: Identify every stitched grid point with the global solution
steps.body: The reference chain starts at \(Y_0\). Inductively assume its state at step \(n\) equals \(Y_{nh}\). The next selected segment begins at that same point, so the local-global uniqueness result identifies its endpoint with \(Y_{nh+h}\). Lean performs induction over the actual chain recursion, checks the finite-horizon inequalities using nonnegative step size, and simplifies the real cast of \(n+1\). The result is the exact identity \(R_n=Y_{nh}\), including zero step size.

steps.title: Identify all intermediate times within a reference segment
steps.body: Once the starting grid point is identified, the same uniqueness result proves \(Z_n(t)=Y_{nh+t}\) throughout the whole segment. This lets a stationary global phase law supply both the stationary reference position at grid points and the Gaussian reference velocity at intermediate times required by the KLMC local-error proof. No stationary law is assumed for a newly invented process: the stitched reference is proved to be the actual global solution.

KineticLangevin/OUMarginal.lean.title: The actual OU innovation law and independent time stream
KineticLangevin/OUMarginal.lean.summary: The canonical convolution is an actual random variable on the constructed Brownian source. This module proves that its fluctuation-dissipation scaling has exactly the thermal Gaussian law, and that full spatial vectors on distinct grid intervals are independent. The complete stream therefore has the independent Gaussian product law required by the concrete Markov transition.

steps.title: Identify independent spatial copies through their actual scalar law
steps.body: A scalar L² variable \(Z\) is evaluated on each independent coordinate Brownian source. Each copy has the same proved law \( u\), and the coordinate product construction proves their independence. The infinite-product law theorem, specialized to finitely many spatial coordinates, gives the finite product measure \( u^{\otimes\iota}\). Transporting this law through the actual Euclidean coordinate map identifies the law of spatialLift; its representative theorem supplies the almost-everywhere equality. For \( u\) equal to a scaled real standard Gaussian, the product pushforward identity and the definition-independent standard Gaussian theorem identify this law as the same scalar scaling of the Euclidean standard Gaussian.

steps.title: Compute the actual scalar thermal variance
steps.body: The scalar segment convolution is the constructed isonormal map applied to its actual time kernel \(K\), so it has centered Gaussian variance \(\|K\|^2\). With \(c=\sqrt{2\gamma}\), its scaled variance is \(2\gamma\|K\|^2\). The proved kernel inner-product identity gives \(\|K\|^2=\int_0^h e^{-2\gamma s}\,ds\), and the exact fluctuation-decay balance gives \(2\gamma\|K\|^2=1-e^{-2\gamma h}\). This equals \(\sigma_h^2\) for \(\sigma_h=\sqrt{1-e^{-2\gamma h}}\). Lean derives nonnegativity from the damping bound, uses the actual isonormal Gaussian law, checks the equality of nonnegative-real variances, and rewrites the scaled real Gaussian pushforward. Zero friction is included without division.

steps.title: Identify the entire spatial OU Gaussian law
steps.body: Apply the independent-spatial-copy result to the proved scalar thermal law. Linearity of spatialLift identifies its scaled scalar input with the actual scaled vector segment convolution. Thus \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\,Z_{a,h}\) has exactly the law of \(\sqrt{1-e^{-2\gamma h}}\,\xi\), where \(\xi\) is the Euclidean standard Gaussian. This proves the full vector distribution rather than only its covariance.

steps.title: Prove independence of actual full-vector innovations across time
steps.body: The canonical KLMC innovation pairs are already proved independent over disjoint time-grid intervals by their actual Brownian kernel supports. Project each pair to its velocity component and apply any fixed scalar scaling. The actual L² vector-segment representatives agree almost everywhere with these projected canonical innovations. Independence is preserved under these measurable projections and almost-everywhere changes. Lean explicitly combines the representative scalar-multiplication event with the canonical endpoint identity.

steps.title: Identify the full independent Gaussian stream
steps.body: Every scaled OU grid innovation has the exact thermal Gaussian law, and the preceding theorem proves independence of all grid vectors. The infinite-product law theorem therefore identifies the entire actual innovation stream with the product of this Gaussian law over all iterations. Measurability follows from the strongly measurable L² representative at each countable grid index. This stream identity is the source-level fact used to transfer the concrete Brownian-driven splitting chain to its iterated Markov laws.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalCoupledSegments.title: The actual canonical KLMC coupling on each initial transport plan
KineticLangevin/CanonicalCoupledSegments.summary: Fix any finite-cost coupling of the initial position law and the target position law. The probability space is its explicit product with an independent standard Gaussian velocity and the canonical vector Brownian source. This module constructs the numerical chain, the exact reference segments and the auxiliary exact segments on that same space, and proves every analytic segment requirement used by the quantitative KLMC theorem.

steps.title: Specify the concrete probability space and source projection
steps.body: The phase variable is velocity first. The sample space contains the two coupled initial positions, one shared Gaussian velocity and one vector Brownian source. The measure is the actual initial-coupling product extension; probability follows from its first marginal and from the Gaussian/Brownian probability factors. The Brownian-source projection preserves its measure. Pullback along that projection gives a continuous linear map on L², and its representative theorem identifies it almost everywhere with evaluation on the actual product sample.

steps.title: Construct the common Brownian input and filtered innovation
steps.body: The scaled source lift includes the physical amplitude \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\). At iteration \(n\), the input is the actual vector Brownian increment on \((nh,nh+t]\), and the filtered input is the exponential response to that same increment. The unscaled innovation pair consists of the exact velocity and position Wiener responses at the step endpoint. Both input paths are continuous in L², and the additive input starts at zero. These follow from the source lift's continuity and linearity and the proved vector-response properties.

steps.title: Identify the exact noise equations and implemented numerical step
steps.body: The constructed filtered input satisfies \(B_n(t)=W_n(t)-\gamma\int_0^tB_n(s)ds\). Its endpoint is the scaled velocity innovation, and its actual time primitive is the scaled positional innovation. Lean transports the vector Brownian equations through the continuous linear source lift and commutes that lift with Bochner integration. Induction on the actual recursions then proves that the exponential-input chain is exactly klmcChain, with the canonical correlated innovation pair and the prescribed fluctuation-dissipation scaling.

steps.title: Connect Brownian L² innovations with the generic output-law construction
steps.body: The L² innovation pair has the same representatives as the pointwise canonical Brownian innovation. The proof pulls back the previously established vector-response representative theorem to the coupling product and combines the two component identities. Comparing with the generic product-law layer's representatives gives equality of the actual L² pairs. Thus the numerical chain analyzed here has the coupling-independent output law already proved for the implemented KLMC chain.

steps.title: Build the actual numerical and stationary-reference initial states
steps.body: The two initial phases share exactly one Gaussian velocity variable. The numerical phase uses the first coupled position; the reference phase uses the second. The reference representative is proved to be the explicit pair \((V,X_\mathrm{ref})\). Product independence and the two marginal laws prove that its actual law is \(\mathcal N(0,I_d)\otimes\pi\). The finite target second moment and finite coupling cost supply the required L² initial positions.

steps.title: Construct all three chains and segment families
steps.body: The numerical chain applies the actual lifted original gradient and the constructed correlated innovations. The reference chain stitches exact selected kinetic segments, each driven by the actual canonical Brownian increment for that iteration. The corresponding reference segments start from these actual reference states. The auxiliary exact segment starts instead from the actual numerical state and receives the identical additive input. The drift is the genuine pointwise gradient lifted to L²; no substitute potential on the L² space is assumed.

steps.title: Prove every analytic premise of the KLMC coupling theorem
steps.body: The bundled specification supplies continuity of auxiliary paths, reference paths and filtered inputs; exact initial states; reference endpoint matching; the implemented exponential update; both actual common-input integral equations; the exponential mild identity; the kinematic primitive identity; and equal initial velocities. Each field follows from the concrete definitions and earlier proved equations. The mild and kinematic fields are derived internally. The only remaining probabilistic input for a final stationary-error theorem is the stationary law of the actual global reference diffusion, proved separately and connected to these stitched segments by uniqueness.

KineticLangevin/LpHamiltonianLaw.lean.title: The actual L² Hamiltonian comparator has the exact Gibbs law
KineticLangevin/LpHamiltonianLaw.lean.summary: This module closes the probabilistic reference obligations for the Hamiltonian part of the OBABO bias argument. It constructs the actual L² Picard flow, identifies its finite-dimensional output law, derives exact Gibbs stationarity and velocity/score moments, and applies the proved local O–Verlet–O comparison. No stationary reference-law or local-error bound is postulated.

steps.title: Identify an L² limit with a pointwise numerical limit
steps.body: Suppose actual L² phase variables \(S_n\) converge to S, and their representatives agree almost everywhere with measurable vector approximants \(f_n\) converging almost everywhere to Y. For any continuous linear functional \(\ell\), the characteristic test \(e^{i\ell(z)}\) has norm one. Bounded dominated convergence identifies the characteristic-function limit of the pointwise approximants, while the proved L² characteristic continuity identifies the limit of the L² variables. Their equality yields \(\mathcal L(S)=\mathcal L(Y)\) through characteristic uniqueness. The next lemma proves the required almost-everywhere correspondence for every actual Verlet iterate by induction from the lifted kick and drift identities. Thus the two convergence arguments refer to precisely the same implemented approximants.

steps.title: Identify the actual coupled representatives almost everywhere
steps.body:
Marginal equality alone is insufficient when the local numerical error must be coupled with the same initial state and thermostat inputs. This stronger result identifies the actual representatives almost everywhere. Each component of an L²-convergent phase sequence converges in measure. The known almost-everywhere equality transfers this convergence to the same pointwise Verlet approximants. Their almost-everywhere convergence also implies convergence in measure, because the source is a probability measure. Uniqueness of the limit in measure therefore gives equality almost everywhere of each component, hence of the phase pair.

Apply this argument to the actual L² Hamiltonian flow and its actual Verlet approximants. The result states that its representative at time t is almost everywhere the finite-dimensional Hamiltonian flow evaluated at the same representative of the initial state. Thus adjoining any initial state or thermostat variable preserves the coupling used in the local comparison; no equality of marginal laws is substituted for a joint-law argument.

steps.title: Construct the true L² Hamiltonian integral flow and identify its law
steps.body: The L² force is the actual Nemytskii lift lpDrift; its global Lipschitz bound permits the existing Picard construction with zero friction and zero noise. Its specification gives a continuous global path, the prescribed initial value, and the actual Hamiltonian integral equation on the finite horizon. Verlet convergence holds in this Banach space. The same vector Verlet maps converge pointwise to the selected finite-dimensional Hamiltonian flow. The proved almost-everywhere pointwise identification and the composition rule for pushforwards give the exact law identity \(\mathcal L(A_t)=(H_t)_\#\mathcal L(A_0)\). This does not infer a pathwise identification from an unproved interchange of representatives and time integrals.

steps.title: Derive stationarity and both moment envelopes from the actual target
steps.body: If the initial phase law is the canonical independent Gaussian-times-Gibbs target, the exact Hamiltonian invariance theorem and the derived output-law identity prove that the actual L² flow has that target law at every time. Projecting the actual integral equation with the continuous linear coordinate maps gives the velocity and kinematic component equations; commuting those maps with Bochner integrals is justified by continuity and interval integrability. Projecting the target law gives standard Gaussian velocity and normalized Gibbs position. The exact Gaussian coordinate calculation therefore yields \(\|V_t\|_{L^2}=\sqrt d\), and the already proved Gibbs score estimate gives \(\|\nabla f(X_t)\|_{L^2}\le\sqrt{Md}\). These are conclusions from the actual law, not supplied moment hypotheses.

steps.title: Apply the local OBABO comparison to this constructed stationary reference
steps.body:
Start the genuine L² Hamiltonian path at the actual first thermostat half-step and assume its phase law is the canonical target, as supplied by thermostat invariance. Its continuity, initial value, velocity equation, kinematic equation, and uniform moments have all been proved above. The local O–Verlet–O versus O–Hamiltonian–O theorem therefore applies with \(C=\sqrt d\) and \(G=\sqrt{Md}\). It yields the actual weighted error bound

\[2h^2\left(\sqrt{Md}+\sqrt M\sqrt d+\frac{h}{4}\sqrt M\sqrt{Md}\right).\]

The two actual thermostat noises are retained, their common final contribution cancels, and the damping needs only \(|\delta|\le1\). This provides the numerical local budget for the global sampling-bias estimate.

KineticLangevin/SplittingTarget.lean.title: Quadratic stationary weak error for the actual kinetic splitting
KineticLangevin/SplittingTarget.lean.summary: This module applies the exact corrected Verlet identity and the exact Gaussian thermostat identity to the actual normalized Gaussian-times-Gibbs target. Averaging a bounded test over the thermostat preserves its bound. The uncorrected splitting therefore has a proved quadratic one-step stationary weak defect, and its actual Markov iterate accumulates at most a linear number of these defects.

steps.title: Use the actual thermal Gaussian innovation measure
steps.body: The additive innovation measure is the pushforward of the Euclidean standard Gaussian by the coefficient \(\sigma_h=\sqrt{1-e^{-2\gamma h}}\). It is a probability measure because it is a measurable pushforward of a probability measure. The preceding OU marginal theorem identifies this exact law with the actual canonical convolution innovation; here it is the concrete measure used by the Markov transition.

steps.title: Normalize the exact corrected Verlet identity
steps.body: The canonical target is an explicitly proved finite scalar normalization of the actual Hamiltonian weighted measure. A density-weighted measure, its measurable pushforward, and their sum all commute with this scalar multiplication. Scaling the earlier exact identity therefore gives \((V_h)_\#(a_h\pi)+R_\#((1-a_h)\pi)=\pi\) for the actual normalized target. Lean rewrites the explicit normalization, both density scalings, both pushforward scalings, and the corrected Hamiltonian Gibbs identity.

steps.title: Derive the normalized target phase moment
steps.body: The unnormalized Hamiltonian measure already has integrable \(\|v\|^2+\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\) from first-order strong convexity and Lipschitz force growth. The explicit normalizing scalar is finite: its Gaussian factor is an ordinary finite real number and its inverse potential partition is finite because the partition is strictly positive. Lean checks these extended-real facts and applies integrability under finite scalar multiplication. Thus the rejection envelope remains an actual finite target moment.

steps.title: Preserve the target with the actual additive OU law
steps.body: The damping \(\delta_h=e^{-\gamma h}\) and innovation scale satisfy \(\delta_h^2+\sigma_h^2=1\). The already proved thermostat result preserves the target when driven by a fresh standard Gaussian. Mapping that Gaussian through \(\sigma_h\) changes its law to the explicit additive innovation measure. Lean proves the coefficient identity, maps the independent product source through this noise scaling, composes the two pushforwards, and obtains exact preservation by the additive OU transition.

steps.title: Apply corrected invariance to the thermostat-averaged test
steps.body: For \(\|F\|\le C\), define \(G(z)=\mathbb E_N[F(O_h(z,N))]\). The actual noise integral makes \(G\) measurable with \(\|G\|\le C\). Exact thermostat invariance gives \(\int G\,d\pi=\int F\,d\pi\), while the actual split transition has expectation \(\int G(V_hz)\,d\pi\). Apply the proved corrected-Verlet weak estimate to \(G\), then integrate the actual quadratic rejection envelope. This gives \[\left\|\int F\,d(P_h\pi)-\int F\,d\pi\right\|\le2Ch^2\frac{M(2M+11)}8\int(\|v\|^2+\|\nabla f(x)\|^2)\,d\pi.\] Lean derives both expectation identities from the actual Markov-step integral formula, checks measurability and boundedness of the averaged test, and composes the checked rejection and target moment estimates.

steps.title: Accumulate only a linear number of genuine local defects
steps.body: The generic Markov test theorem applies the one-step estimate to each iterated dual test, whose bound remains \(C\), and telescopes their expectations under the fixed target. Consequently the actual \(n\)-step splitting law has weak error at most \(n\) times the displayed quadratic defect. Lean verifies nonnegativity of the target moment and all scalar coefficients, supplies the concrete measurable transition, and instantiates the proved generic theorem. With \(h=T/n\), this actual error tends to zero.

KineticLangevin/SplittingLaw.lean.title: The actual splitting chain has its independent-noise Markov law
KineticLangevin/SplittingLaw.lean.summary: A law identity must be established for the random variables actually used by the construction.
