The input here is the complete joint law of the initial phase and the entire innovation stream. Composing this law with the measurable implemented recursion proves the endpoint law. The same identity is then established for the genuine L² implementation using its proved almost-everywhere representatives.

steps.title: Push the full input law through the actual recursion
steps.body: Let \(C_n(z,w)\) be the explicit recursion run for \(n\) steps. Its joint measurability has already been proved by induction. If \((X,(N_k)_k)\) has the product law \(\pi\otimes Q^{\otimes\mathbb N}\), the pushforward composition rule says its output has law \((\pi\otimes Q^{\otimes\mathbb N})\circ C_n^{-1}\). The existing finite-prefix proof identifies this with the actual iterated Markov law \(\pi P^n\). On an explicit initial-law/source product, the initial phase and a source stream are independent by the product pushforward identity. Lean proves both statements directly using HasLaw.comp and Measure.map_prod_map.

steps.title: Match the two concrete implementations step for step
steps.body: kineticSplitNoiseChain uses Verlet followed by the exact OU update. Induction shows it is precisely noiseDrivenChain for that step. Continuity of the force makes every kick, drift and thermostat continuous, so their composition is measurable. The law theorem can therefore be applied to the actual splitting map, with no additional transition-measurability premise.

steps.title: Eliminate the choice of L² representatives
steps.body: The lifted chain has already been proved equal almost everywhere to the pointwise vector chain with the same initial state and innovations. Replace its pushforward using this equality, then apply the full-input-law theorem. This proves the actual L² endpoint law is the independent-noise Markov iterate. Quotient representatives cannot create an extra source of randomness or change the chain law.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalProduct.lean.title: A concrete independent initial phase and canonical Brownian source
KineticLangevin/CanonicalProduct.lean.summary: The stationarity proof takes place on one explicit probability space: the product of an initial phase law and the constructed vector Brownian source. This module builds the actual initial L² variables, the actual continuous Brownian forcing and its OU-filtered innovations, then proves the complete initial/noise joint law. The resulting splitting law identity has no assumed independence or Gaussian marginal fields.

steps.title: Represent the original initial phase on the product source
steps.body: H is the finite-dimensional Euclidean state, and Sample pairs a phase with a vector Brownian sample. The probability measure is exactly \(\pi\otimes P_B\). Pull the velocity and position projections through the first product projection. Their square integrability follows from that of the original phase law. The two toLp representative identities prove that the resulting phase agrees almost everywhere with the original initial coordinate.

steps.title: Lift the actual continuous Brownian input
steps.body: The second product projection preserves the Brownian source law. Its pullback is a linear isometry on L², hence a continuous linear map. Apply it to \(\sqrt{2\gamma}B_t\), where the constructed Brownian input is continuous in L² and zero at time zero. Linearity and continuity give the same properties after adjoining the independent initial phase. Thus the forcing used by the deterministic integral solver is an actual Brownian forcing on this very source.

steps.title: Use the exact OU-filtered Brownian intervals
steps.body: The innovation in interval \([nh,(n+1)h]\) is the pulled-back isonormal convolution \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\int_{nh}^{(n+1)h}e^{-\gamma((n+1)h-s)}dB_s\). Its representative is exactly the original source variable composed with the Brownian projection. Continuous linear maps commute with the deterministic OU filter. Combined with the proved canonical integration-by-parts identity, this shows the continuous-input filter is exactly this innovation, not merely a random variable with a matching covariance.

steps.title: Derive the complete independent Gaussian stream law
steps.body: The canonical OU marginal theorem gives covariance \((1-e^{-2\gamma h})I\); the disjoint-interval theorem gives independence of the full vector innovations across time. Their whole stream therefore has the infinite product of the thermal Gaussian law. The explicit initial-law/source product makes the initial phase independent of that entire stream. Finally use the almost-everywhere initial and innovation identities to obtain the complete joint law of the actual L² variables.

steps.title: Identify both actual splitting endpoint laws
steps.body: Apply the proved full-input-law theorem to the actual lifted Verlet–OU chain. Its phase pushforward is exactly the Markov iterate with fresh thermal Gaussian OU innovations and initial law \(\pi\). The exact OU-filter identity also identifies the continuous-input chain with the same noise-driven chain, so its endpoint has that law as well. These identities provide the missing connection between the pathwise convergence theorem and the measure-level weak stationarity calculation.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalGlobalSegments..title: One canonical global kinetic reference behind all coupling segments
KineticLangevin/CanonicalGlobalSegments..summary: The exact reference segments are constructed on one canonical Brownian source. This module identifies their increment input with the increments of one full L² Brownian input and proves that every stitched reference state and intermediate segment point belongs to the actual full kinetic solution.

steps.title: Construct the full canonical input and identify its increments
steps.body: The full input is the scalar canonical Brownian value assembled spatially and pulled onto the actual initial-coupling extension with amplitude \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\). It is continuous in L² because each assembly and pullback is continuous linear. The Brownian value at zero vanishes: Lean verifies that its deterministic time indicator has empty support, then uses linearity of the isonormal map. For nonnegative local time, the constructed segment input equals the full input difference at \(nh+t\) and \(nh\). The proof checks the nonnegative real-to-NNReal casts and uses linearity of spatial assembly and source pullback.

steps.title: Construct the actual full reference solution
steps.body: The global reference is the selected kinetic solution with the genuine lifted gradient, the canonical reference initial phase and the full canonical Brownian input. Its specification proves continuity, its exact starting phase, and the actual kinetic integral equation over the whole finite horizon. There is no stationary-law requirement in its definition.

steps.title: Identify every stitched reference point by uniqueness
steps.body: The generic stitching theorem now applies because the local inputs are proved to be actual increments of the full input. Consequently \(R_n=Y_{nh}\), and \(Z_n(t)=Y_{nh+t}\) throughout each step whose endpoint lies in the global horizon. Lean instantiates the existing exact uniqueness results with the actual L² gradient and checks the horizon arithmetic. Thus a stationary law for the full constructed kinetic solution supplies the law of all reference states used by the quantitative KLMC proof.

KineticLangevin/RandomMapPerturbation.le.title: Pass explicit local kernel errors through the true coupling infimum
KineticLangevin/RandomMapPerturbation.le.summary: These transport lemmas connect actual measurable random maps to their iterated independent-noise laws. They preserve every marginal and take the actual infimum over initial couplings. Their inputs are a pathwise contraction and the measured L² discrepancy between two explicit maps; these analytic inputs are proved separately for OBABO and its Hamiltonian comparator.

steps.title: Extend every coupling by a common independent innovation
steps.body:
Given any input coupling \(c\) of \(\mu, u\), append one independent innovation with law Q. Let the numerical output be \(F(x,s)\) and the comparator output be \(G(y,s)\). Their difference decomposes exactly as

\[F(x,s)-G(y,s)=[F(x,s)-F(y,s)]-[G(y,s)-F(y,s)].\]

Minkowski and the pathwise contraction bound the first term by q times the original coupling cost. The law of \((y,s)\) is proved to be exactly \( u\otimes Q\); the pushforward formula for L² therefore identifies the second term with the actual local discrepancy under that fixed product law. Both output marginals are the actual random-map laws. The resulting bound holds for every c, so the established affine-infimum theorem gives \(W_2(F_\#(\mu\otimes Q),G_\#( u\otimes Q))\le qW_2(\mu, u)+b\). No optimal-coupling existence is assumed.

steps.title: Iterate the actual Markov laws against an invariant comparator
steps.body:
Suppose the explicit comparator map preserves \(\pi\) under the independent source Q and its actual local L² error is at most b. Applying the preceding transport theorem at every numerical iteration gives \(e_{n+1}\le qe_n+b\). The proof first establishes that each iterated law is a probability and that every transport distance is finite, using the extended-real recurrence and finite initial distance. Only then does it convert to real distances. The proved geometric recurrence yields

\[W_2(\mu_n,\pi)\le q^nW_2(\mu_0,\pi)+\frac{b}{1-q},\qquad0\le q<1.\]

This general lemma keeps the invariant-map and integrated-local-error obligations explicit. The Hamiltonian and local-state modules supply them for the actual OBABO comparison; the convergence theorem itself is not used as an input.

steps.title: Expose finite output transport before taking real values
steps.body: The extended affine one-step bound also proves finite output distance at every actual Markov iteration. Start with finite initial transport. At each step the finite nonnegative coefficient times the preceding finite distance, plus the finite local budget, is finite. The actual distance lies below that finite quantity. This induction is exposed separately so coordinate projections and mean-square consequences can use a real Wasserstein estimate without silently converting infinity to zero.

KineticLangevin/StationarityTransfer.lea.title: Exact kinetic Gibbs stationarity from the actual initial/noise laws
KineticLangevin/StationarityTransfer.lea.summary: This theorem assembles the full analytic stationarity limit. It starts with an actual continuous L² kinetic integral solution. Its explicit input-law premise states the independent target initial phase and complete canonical OU innovation stream; concrete product-source modules derive that premise. Numerical convergence, stationary weak defects, actual output-law transfer, and the final invariant law are all proved inside the theorem.

steps.title: Derive exact stationarity through the actual splitting limit
steps.body:
Let \(\pi\) be the actual normalized Gaussian-times-Gibbs target, and let \(Y\) solve the actual kinetic integral equation driven by the continuous L² input \(B\). On a mesh \(h_n=T/(n+1)\), form the concrete Verlet–OU approximation \(S_n\) using the filtered increments of this same \(B\). The proved Banach splitting theorem gives \(S_n\to Y_T\) in the actual product of L² spaces.

The full initial/innovation joint law is the explicit product \(\pi\otimes Q_{h_n}^{\otimes\mathbb N}\). The checked source-law transfer theorem, together with the almost-everywhere vector-chain representation, identifies the actual law of \(S_n\) with the implemented Markov iterate. Its bounded-test error is at most \[2(n+1)h_n^2 K A=\frac{2T^2KA}{n+1},\qquad K=\frac{M(2M+11)}8,\quad A=\int(\|v\|^2+\|\nabla f(x)\|^2)\,d\pi.\] The moment is finite by the proved target tail theorem. The mesh is eventually at most one, so every quadratic rejection estimate applies, and the displayed scalar error tends to zero.

The actual phase-law continuity theorem now identifies the L² limiting phase law with \(\pi\). Lean constructs the true approximation sequence, applies the proved convergence theorem, rewrites its chain law using the explicit initial/noise product distribution, rewrites the bounded test expectation through the actual pushforward, invokes the proved Markov weak-error bound, and checks the scalar \(T^2/(n+1)\) decay. It then applies dual-characteristic uniqueness for finite measures. No stationary solution, local-error conclusion, output-law independence field, or numerical-limit conclusion is assumed. The remaining input-law hypothesis is a concrete source probability identity, supplied by the canonical independent-product construction.

KineticLangevin/LpWeightedGeometry.lean.title: Identify weighted phase L² errors with actual finite-dimensional costs
KineticLangevin/LpWeightedGeometry.lean.summary: A local estimate in a pair of L² spaces must refer to the same Euclidean phase geometry as the vector sampler. This module constructs the explicit L² Euclidean pair and proves its exact norm and representative identities. It then proves that the actual weighted representative cost is precisely the weighted phase norm used by the local analysis.

steps.title: Construct a genuine Euclidean phase variable in L²
steps.body: The coordinate injections \(u\mapsto(u,0)\), \(w\mapsto(0,w)\) are continuous linear maps into WithLp 2 (E × E). Lift each through compLpL and add their outputs. Almost-everywhere identities for lifted linear maps and L² addition show that the resulting variable represents exactly \((A(\omega),B(\omega))\). Expand its L² inner product as an integral, use the Euclidean product inner product pointwise, and split the two integrable self-inner-products. This proves \(\|\operatorname{pair}(A,B)\|_{L^2}^2=\|A\|_{L^2}^2+\|B\|_{L^2}^2\). Thus the construction uses the Euclidean geometry, not the default maximum norm of an ordinary product.

steps.title: Lift the weighted transform without changing its norm
steps.body:
Apply the Euclidean pair construction to \(X+bV\) and \(\sqrt{a-b^2}V\). The actual representative is almost everywhere the original vector weighted transform \(T(V(\omega),X(\omega))\), with all addition and scalar-multiplication representatives justified explicitly. The squared norm identity for the pair is exactly the defining squared norm of the weighted phase transform on the L² Hilbert space. Both norms are nonnegative, so equality of their squares gives equality of the norms. Finally the standard L² norm definition and finiteness of an actual L² variable give

\[\|T(V(\cdot),X(\cdot))\|_{L^2}=\|(V,X)\|_E.\]

The formal statement retains extended-real L² norms on the left and converts the finite actual norm with ENNReal.ofReal. This is the needed bridge from local Hilbert estimates to true coupling costs.

steps.title: Keep differences and the entire OBABO step tied to their actual representatives
steps.body: The first lemma records the almost-everywhere representative of a phase difference, using the two component subtraction identities. The second expands OBABO into first thermostat, Verlet, and final thermostat, then composes the already proved representative identities for all three. Consequently the lifted nonlinear force update represents exactly the original finite-dimensional O-B-A-B-O sampler with the same two supplied noise variables. These equalities preserve the joint coupling; a marginal-law equality is never substituted for the actual common-noise realization.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalReferenceNoise..title: The actual initial phase and Brownian innovation joint law
KineticLangevin/CanonicalReferenceNoise..summary: The Gibbs stationarity proof needs the real joint law of the initial phase and all future filtered Brownian increments. This module derives that law on each arbitrary initial-position coupling extension. steps.title: Project the coupling source onto an independent phase/Brownian product

KineticLangevin/GenericCanonicalKLMC.lea.summary: The entire actual-source KLMC proof is stated for a general finite coordinate type \(I\). This includes the particle index \(\{\theta\}\sqcup(\{1,\ldots,N\}\times\{x\})\) without a separate coordinate-isometry transport. All initial couplings, canonical Brownian inputs, selected reference flows, Gibbs stationary laws and genuine Wasserstein infima are the same concrete constructions as in the finite-dimension presentation; the dimension in the final bias is exactly \(|I|\).

steps.title: Specify the concrete probability space and source projection
steps.body: The phase variable is velocity first. The sample space contains the two coupled initial positions, one shared Gaussian velocity and one vector Brownian source. The measure is the actual initial-coupling product extension; probability follows from its first marginal and from the Gaussian/Brownian probability factors. The Brownian-source projection preserves its measure. Pullback along that projection gives a continuous linear map on L², and its representative theorem identifies it almost everywhere with evaluation on the actual product sample.

steps.title: Construct the common Brownian input and filtered innovation
steps.body: The scaled source lift includes the physical amplitude \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\). At iteration \(n\), the input is the actual vector Brownian increment on \((nh,nh+t]\), and the filtered input is the exponential response to that same increment. The unscaled innovation pair consists of the exact velocity and position Wiener responses at the step endpoint. Both input paths are continuous in L², and the additive input starts at zero. These follow from the source lift's continuity and linearity and the proved vector-response properties.

steps.title: Identify the exact noise equations and implemented numerical step
steps.body: The constructed filtered input satisfies \(B_n(t)=W_n(t)-\gamma\int_0^tB_n(s)ds\). Its endpoint is the scaled velocity innovation, and its actual time primitive is the scaled positional innovation. Lean transports the vector Brownian equations through the continuous linear source lift and commutes that lift with Bochner integration. Induction on the actual recursions then proves that the exponential-input chain is exactly klmcChain, with the canonical correlated innovation pair and the prescribed fluctuation-dissipation scaling.

steps.title: Connect Brownian L² innovations with the generic output-law construction
steps.body: The L² innovation pair has the same representatives as the pointwise canonical Brownian innovation. The proof pulls back the previously established vector-response representative theorem to the coupling product and combines the two component identities. Comparing with the generic product-law layer's representatives gives equality of the actual L² pairs. Thus the numerical chain analyzed here has the coupling-independent output law already proved for the implemented KLMC chain.

steps.title: Build the actual numerical and stationary-reference initial states
steps.body: The two initial phases share exactly one Gaussian velocity variable. The numerical phase uses the first coupled position; the reference phase uses the second. The reference representative is proved to be the explicit pair \((V,X_\mathrm{ref})\). Product independence and the two marginal laws prove that its actual law is \(\mathcal N(0,I_{|I|})\otimes\pi\). The finite target second moment and finite coupling cost supply the required L² initial positions.

steps.title: Construct all three chains and segment families
steps.body: The numerical chain applies the actual lifted original gradient and the constructed correlated innovations. The reference chain stitches exact selected kinetic segments, each driven by the actual canonical Brownian increment for that iteration. The corresponding reference segments start from these actual reference states. The auxiliary exact segment starts instead from the actual numerical state and receives the identical additive input. The drift is the genuine pointwise gradient lifted to L²; no substitute potential on the L² space is assumed.

steps.title: Prove every analytic premise of the KLMC coupling theorem
steps.body: The bundled specification supplies continuity of auxiliary paths, reference paths and filtered inputs; exact initial states; reference endpoint matching; the implemented exponential update; both actual common-input integral equations; the exponential mild identity; the kinematic primitive identity; and equal initial velocities. Each field follows from the concrete definitions and earlier proved equations. The mild and kinematic fields are derived internally. The only remaining probabilistic input for a final stationary-error theorem is the stationary law of the actual global reference diffusion, proved separately and connected to these stitched segments by uniqueness.

steps.title: Construct the full canonical input and identify its increments
steps.body: The full input is the scalar canonical Brownian value assembled spatially and pulled onto the actual initial-coupling extension with amplitude \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\). It is continuous in L² because each assembly and pullback is continuous linear. The Brownian value at zero vanishes: Lean verifies that its deterministic time indicator has empty support, then uses linearity of the isonormal map. For nonnegative local time, the constructed segment input equals the full input difference at \(nh+t\) and \(nh\). The proof checks the nonnegative real-to-NNReal casts and uses linearity of spatial assembly and source pullback.

steps.title: Construct the actual full reference solution
steps.body: The global reference is the selected kinetic solution with the genuine lifted gradient, the canonical reference initial phase and the full canonical Brownian input. Its specification proves continuity, its exact starting phase, and the actual kinetic integral equation over the whole finite horizon. There is no stationary-law requirement in its definition.

steps.title: Identify every stitched reference point by uniqueness
steps.body: The generic stitching theorem now applies because the local inputs are proved to be actual increments of the full input. Consequently \(R_n=Y_{nh}\), and \(Z_n(t)=Y_{nh+t}\) throughout each step whose endpoint lies in the global horizon. Lean instantiates the existing exact uniqueness results with the actual L² gradient and checks the horizon arithmetic. Thus a stationary law for the full constructed kinetic solution supplies the law of all reference states used by the quantitative KLMC proof.

steps.title: Project the coupling source onto an independent phase/Brownian product
steps.body: The projection sends the full sample to \(((V,X_\mathrm{ref}),\omega_\mathrm{Brownian})\). Its law is \((\mathcal N(0,I_{|I|})\otimes\pi)\otimes P_\mathrm{Brownian}\). Lean first projects the initial coupling onto its second marginal, retaining the independent Gaussian/Brownian source. It then applies measure-preserving product associativity and swaps the position and velocity factors. Thus independence of the complete reference initial phase and the complete Brownian source is proved for the actual product construction.

steps.title: Identify the actual full-input OU increment
steps.body: The deterministic integration-by-parts input used in the kinetic splitting proof is \(\Delta W-\gamma\int_0^he^{-\gamma(h-s)}\Delta W_sds\). The actual local-input increment identity replaces each difference of the full canonical input by its constructed segment input. Applying the vector exponential-response formula through the continuous linear source lift proves that this OU increment is exactly the filtered velocity response. Its representative is consequently the scaled canonical vector response on the original Brownian source, pulled onto the coupling extension.

steps.title: Derive the full independent thermal Gaussian joint law
steps.body: The vector OU stream already has the exact iid Gaussian law with scale \(\sqrt{1-\psi_0(h)^2}\). The product-source joint-law theorem combines this stream with the initial phase target. Composition with the proved phase/Brownian projection law transfers that product law to the actual coupling extension. Finally, the representative identities identify its initial phase with the constructed reference initial L² phase and its stream with the actual full-input OU increments. The resulting joint law is precisely the source obligation of the proved kinetic Gibbs stationarity transfer theorem.

steps.title: Fix the actual numerical output law
steps.body: The definition uses the original pointwise KLMC method, the standard Gaussian initial velocity and the exact canonical correlated Brownian innovations. The numerical L² chain is identified with the generic product-law construction by equality of the actual innovation variables. The established output-law theorem then proves that its pushforward is independent of which initial position coupling was chosen.

steps.title: Transfer one actual global stationary phase law to the reference segments
steps.body: The named stationary property concerns the full constructed kinetic flow: at every time its phase law is \(\mathcal N(0,I_{|I|})\otimes\pi\). It contains no numerical convergence conclusion. Exact chain-to-global identification transfers its position marginal to every reference grid point. Exact segment-to-global identification transfers its Gaussian velocity marginal to every intermediate time in a reference segment. Lean obtains these marginals by composition with the product-measure projections.

steps.title: Apply the proved coupling estimate to one actual initial plan
steps.body: The initial position L² discrepancy equals the true cost of the supplied transport coupling; this follows from the concrete extension's representative and norm identities. The segment specification furnishes all analytic local-error premises internally. Together with the derived stationary position and Gaussian velocity marginals, the quantitative L² KLMC theorem gives \(W_2(\nu_n,\pi)\le\sqrt2(1-3mh/(4\gamma))^n\operatorname{cost}(c)+Mh\sqrt{2|I|}/m\). Output-law equality and initial-cost equality rewrite this into a bound for the actual numerical law.

steps.title: Prove output finiteness and take the transport infimum
steps.body: Finite initial Wasserstein distance supplies an actual finite-cost initial coupling. Its numerical and reference states are genuine L² variables, so their distance gives a finite transport bound on the output law. This proves output finiteness before real-valued transport arithmetic is used. The scalar recurrence estimate proves the contraction factor is nonnegative under the paper's step restrictions. Lean then applies the proved infimum theorem over all finite-cost couplings, obtaining the same estimate with \(W_2(\mu,\pi)\) in place of the cost of a chosen plan. No existence of an optimal coupling is assumed.

steps.title: Prove Gibbs stationarity of the actual global coupling reference
steps.body: The reference begins with standard Gaussian velocity independent of the target Gibbs position. Its full Brownian forcing and its entire filtered innovation stream are actual constructed objects on the initial-coupling extension. Their exact initial/noise product law is already proved. The kinetic stationarity transfer theorem therefore applies directly to the actual integral solution. For a time \(t\) inside a larger horizon, Lean restricts the actual integral equation to \([0,t]\), supplies the continuous input and its zero starting value, and applies the proved splitting-limit stationarity result. This yields the full phase law \(\mathcal N(0,I_{|I|})\otimes\pi\) at every reference time, without a remaining stationarity or Gaussian-marginal hypothesis.

steps.title: Conclude the source-paper KLMC Wasserstein estimate
steps.body: Let \(f\) be differentiable, \(m\)-strongly convex with \(m>0\), and have an \(M\)-Lipschitz gradient. If \(\gamma^2\ge m+M\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(0

KineticLangevin/OBABOPosition.lean.title: The original OBABO position laws satisfy the full sampling bound
KineticLangevin/OBABOPosition.lean.summary: The actual initial phase law is standard Gaussian velocity independent of the specified position law. Coupling these velocities identically costs nothing. The explicit inverse weighted coordinate map then projects the proved full Markov theorem to the actual position laws, with factor √2 and finite output transport established separately.

steps.title: Project the contracting geometry to the physical position
steps.body: The projection is the position coordinate of the explicitly verified inverse transform. The metric lower bound gives \(\|x-y\|^2\le2\|T(v,x)-T(w,y)\|^2\). Both sides are nonnegative, so the square comparison yields the global √2 Lipschitz coefficient. Composing this projection with the original weighted transform is exactly the ordinary position projection; this is proved from the inverse identity, not supplied as a law equivalence.

steps.title: Adjoin the same Gaussian velocity to every initial position coupling
steps.body: For every coupling of two position laws, append one common independent Gaussian velocity. Their phase difference has zero velocity, so its weighted energy is exactly the squared original position distance. The cross-space random-map theorem takes the actual coupling infimum and yields \(W_{2,E}(\mathcal N\otimes\mu,\mathcal N\otimes\nu)\le W_2(\mu,\nu)\). Product-measure swapping proves that the actual pushforward initialization is the stated independent Gaussian-times-position law. No optimal position coupling is assumed.

steps.title: Obtain the unconditional actual position estimate and expose finite transport
steps.body:
Start from \(\mathcal N(0,I_d)\otimes\mu\), use the actual independent Gaussian-pair OBABO transition at every step, and let \( u_n\) be its actual position marginal. Under the original strong-convexity, smoothness, friction and step-size restrictions, the theorem proves both finite \(W_2( u_n,\pi)\) and

\[W_2( u_n,\pi)\le\sqrt2\,r^nW_2(\mu,\pi)+ rac{6\sqrt2\gamma}{m}h\sqrt d\left(4\sqrt M+ rac{Mh}{2} ight),\qquad r=\sqrt{1- rac{mh}{3\gamma}}.\]

The initial weighted distance is bounded by the actual initial position distance using the preceding shared-velocity construction. The full weighted theorem and its finite-output counterpart apply to the implemented Markov laws. The √2 Lipschitz transport theorem projects both actual output measures; the target projection is the already proved normalized Gibbs marginal. Output finiteness is proved before the real-valued inequality is used, so this endpoint can safely imply RMS consequences. The finite-dimensional index type is arbitrary, allowing direct reuse for the scaled particle configuration.

KineticLangevin/GaussianTail.lean.title: Derive the chi-square positive-part tail from the Gaussian density
KineticLangevin/GaussianTail.lean.summary: The Hessian comparison needs a Gaussian tail estimate even when the Gaussian velocity and position discrepancy are dependent. The relevant bound is \(\mathbb E(\lVert G\rVert^2-a)_+\le4e^{-(a-p)/4}\) for \(a\ge5p\). The proof below derives its exponential moment and the tail estimate from actual Gaussian measures.

steps.title: Compute the scalar exponential square moment with its integrability
steps.body: Multiply the standard Gaussian density by \(e^{x^2/3}\). Its exponent becomes \(-x^2/2+x^2/3=-x^2/6\). The real Gaussian integral therefore gives \(\mathbb Ee^{G^2/3}=\sqrt3\). The proof establishes integrability of this weighted density before computing its integral, so the Bochner integral cannot conceal divergence. Lean uses the actual Gaussian density, the with-density integrability equivalence, the real Gaussian integral and exact square-root algebra.

steps.title: Multiply the independent coordinate moments
steps.body: Since \(e^{\lVert G\rVert^2/3}=\prod_i e^{G_i^2/3}\), product integrability and finite-product Fubini give \(\mathbb Ee^{\lVert G\rVert^2/3}=(\sqrt3)^p\). The proof works on the constructed product of scalar Gaussian measures and uses its established Euclidean standard-Gaussian pushforward. This handles dimension zero as well.

steps.title: Choose an elementary Chernoff tilt
steps.body: The elementary bound \(e^u\ge1+u\) at \(u=1/3\), raised to the fourth power, proves \(\sqrt3\le e^{2/3}\). Also \((y-a)_+\le3e^{(y-a)/3}\), since its positive branch is bounded using the same exponential inequality and its zero branch is nonnegative. These two inequalities give a convenient exponential moment estimate without importing an unproved chi-square concentration result.

steps.title: Integrate the positive-part bound and use the threshold
steps.body: Applying the pointwise bound to \(y=\lVert G\rVert^2\) gives \(\mathbb E(y-a)_+\le3e^{-a/3}(\sqrt3)^p\le3e^{-a/3+2p/3}\). If \(a\ge5p\), the exponent is at most \(-(a-p)/4\). Replacing the factor three by four yields exactly the source bound. Lean first derives integrability of the positive part from its integrable exponential majorant, then applies integral monotonicity, the exact moment and scalar exponent comparison.

steps.title: Use the bound on the original coupled probability space
steps.body: The pushforward integration identity transfers the estimate to any actual standard-Gaussian velocity. Its joint distribution with a numerical position discrepancy is unrestricted. This is essential for a synchronous sampling proof, where past noise generally makes those two variables dependent.

KineticLangevin/ProductContinuousFlow.le.title: Actual continuous kinetic laws and the true Wasserstein infimum
KineticLangevin/ProductContinuousFlow.le.summary: The initial position is independent of a common source carrying the initial velocity and continuous forcing. This construction makes the output law independent of any chosen coupling. We then couple two initial position laws, pull their genuine kinetic solutions onto the same source, and apply the proved arbitrary-shift kinetic energy contraction. Taking the infimum over all initial couplings gives the actual Wasserstein estimate.

steps.title: Construct the actual independent-source diffusion
steps.body: The probability space is the product of the initial position law and the common source. The first L² coordinate is the pulled-back velocity; the second is the original position coordinate. Pulling back the continuous additive forcing gives the genuine kinetic input. The selected Picard solution is then pushed forward at the terminal time to define the position law. The solution specification proves continuity, the exact initial condition and both integral equations. Measurability makes the output a probability measure, and its L² construction proves a finite second moment.

steps.title: Put any initial coupling on the same source
steps.body: Adjoin the same independent source to an arbitrary coupling of the two initial position distributions. The two projections recover the original independent-source spaces exactly, so they preserve measure. Composition of L² pullbacks shows that both projected solutions receive exactly the same velocity and forcing. The representative formula identifies their initial positions with the two original coupling coordinates.

steps.title: Prove the actual bound before taking an infimum
steps.body: The source-pullback theorem transforms each genuine solution equation to the coupling extension. Their common velocity and noise cancel, so the arbitrary-shift L² contraction theorem applies. The initial position L² norm equals the actual root-mean-square transport cost of the supplied coupling: the independent extra source contributes a factor one. At the endpoint, measure-preserving projection recovers each independently defined output law. The L² transport inequality therefore gives the stated bound for this particular initial coupling.

steps.title: Pass to the genuine Wasserstein distance
steps.body: Both initial laws and both output laws have finite second moments. The prefactor is nonnegative because the shifted damping denominator is positive. The proved affine bound over every finite-cost initial coupling therefore passes to the actual infimum defining Wasserstein distance. The result has the paper’s full arbitrary-shift exponential factor and holds for any common square-integrable velocity and any genuine continuous common input, so Brownian forcing is a direct specialization.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalContinuousMixin.title: Theorem 1 for actual Brownian kinetic diffusions
KineticLangevin/CanonicalContinuousMixin.summary: The continuous mixing theorem is instantiated with the existing genuine vector Brownian source. Its initial velocity distribution is arbitrary, subject only to a finite second moment, and is independent of the initial positions and Brownian noise. The output measures are actual terminal pushforwards of the selected kinetic integral solution, on any finite coordinate set.

steps.title: Construct arbitrary initial velocity and genuine Brownian forcing
steps.body: The source is the independent product of the prescribed velocity distribution and the canonical vector Brownian measure. Its first projection gives the actual L² initial velocity. The second projection pulls back the canonical Brownian process, multiplied by the fluctuation-dissipation factor \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\). Continuity and the zero initial value follow from the corresponding proved Brownian facts and linear source pullback.

steps.title: Define the actual position laws and prove arbitrary-shift mixing
steps.body: For each initial position distribution, the independent-source construction solves the actual kinetic equation with the original gradient and genuine Brownian input. Its terminal position pushforward defines the law. Applying the general product-source coupling theorem proves the complete arbitrary-shift exponential coefficient. The common velocity law needs no Gaussian assumption. The initial transport term is the true Wasserstein distance between the initial position distributions, obtained by infimizing over genuine couplings rather than assuming an optimizer or a prescribed coupling cost.

KineticLangevin/GaussianTruncation.lean.title: A checked Gaussian truncation bound with dependent position and velocity
KineticLangevin/GaussianTruncation.lean.summary: A Hessian difference can be small through its spatial Lipschitz bound and uniformly bounded through the Hessian norm bound. This module combines those two genuine pointwise controls with the actual Gaussian velocity tail. The coupled position and velocity may be dependent; no independence premise is used.

steps.title: Separate the moderate velocity region from the exact Gaussian excess
steps.body: Suppose \(d\le\min\{B,Lx\}\,v\), with all quantities nonnegative. For a cutoff \(a\ge0\), the exact scalar estimate is \[d^2\le L^2ax^2+B^2(v^2-a)_+.\] Put \(k=\min\{B,Lx\}\). Where \(v^2\le a\), use \(k\le Lx\) and \(d^2\le k^2v^2\le L^2x^2a\). Where \(v^2>a\), write \(k^2v^2=k^2a+k^2(v^2-a)\), use \(k\le Lx\) in the first term and \(k\le B\) in the second. Lean proves the two squared bounds from the nonnegative minimum, splits on the cutoff comparison, rewrites the positive part in each region, and applies these two scalar comparisons. The subtraction of \(a\) in the tail term is retained exactly, which permits the sharp positive-part tail bound.

steps.title: Identify actual Hilbert L² norms with their actual second moments
steps.body: For an actual Hilbert-valued L² element \(X\), \(\|X\|_{L^2}^2=\int\|X(\omega)\|^2\,dP\). Lean rewrites the squared norm as the real inner product of \(X\) with itself, unfolds the actual L² inner product as its Bochner integral, and rewrites the pointwise inner products as squared norms. This gives the precise identity needed to integrate the scalar cutoff estimate; it does not replace a possibly divergent moment by a totalized real expression.

steps.title: Integrate the cutoff and use only the actual Gaussian velocity marginal
steps.body:
Let \(D,X,V\) be actual Euclidean L² random variables on one probability space, and suppose \(V\) has the actual standard Gaussian law in dimension \(p\). Assume \(\|D\|\le\min\{B,L\|X\|\}\|V\|\) almost everywhere. The preceding scalar inequality integrates to \[\|D\|_{L^2}^2\le L^2a\|X\|_{L^2}^2+B^2\mathbb E(\|V\|^2-a)_+.\] Lean proves integrability of the velocity positive part directly from the actual L² moment, proves integrability of both terms on the right, and applies almost-everywhere monotonicity of the Bochner integral.

The checked Gaussian tail theorem, transferred through the actual velocity law, gives \(\mathbb E(\|V\|^2-a)_+\le4e^{-(a-p)/4}\) for \(a\ge5p\). Hence \[\|D\|_{L^2}\le L\sqrt a\,\|X\|_{L^2}+2B e^{-(a-p)/8}.\] Lean checks the exponential-square identity, compares the two nonnegative squares, and bounds the nonnegative cross term. The only probability fact used is the marginal law of \(V\); arbitrary dependence between \(X\), \(D\), and \(V\) is retained throughout. This is the cutoff estimate required for a random Hessian-difference factor multiplying a stationary Gaussian velocity.

KineticLangevin/HessianRemainder.lean.title: The genuine quadratic Taylor remainder
KineticLangevin/HessianRemainder.lean.summary: The second-order integrator linearizes the force at its initial position. Its error requires a quadratic estimate for this actual linearization, obtained from the explicitly integrated Hessian along a segment. The derivative and Hessian Lipschitz assumptions are ordinary analytic hypotheses on the force.

steps.title: Integrate Hessian variation along the segment
steps.body: The averaged Hessian is the Bochner integral of H(y+t(x−y)), with t between zero and one. Subtracting H(y) inside the integral gives an integrand with norm at most M₂t‖x−y‖. The norm of an integral is at most the integral of this nonnegative envelope, whose value is M₂‖x−y‖/2. Lean checks continuity of the integrand, moves subtraction through the integral, applies the Lipschitz inequality on the segment, and evaluates the elementary integral of t.

steps.title: Apply the averaged operator to the displacement
steps.body: The fundamental theorem of calculus identifies g(x)−g(y) with the averaged Hessian applied to x−y. Thus the true Taylor remainder equals (H̄−H(y))(x−y). The operator norm inequality bounds this by ‖H̄−H(y)‖‖x−y‖, yielding M₂‖x−y‖²/2. This is an actual remainder estimate; the Hessian is never replaced by an assumed scalar or a fictitious common mean-value point.

KineticLangevin/RandomOperatorLp.lean.title: Bounded random Hessians act on L²
KineticLangevin/RandomOperatorLp.lean.summary: A Hessian evaluated at a random initial position is itself random. To use it inside Bochner time integrals, we construct its genuine continuous linear action on square-integrable random vectors. The operator may depend on every coupled variable; independence is unnecessary.

steps.title: Construct the action by Hölder multiplication
steps.body: A measurable operator field A with a deterministic bound ‖A(ω)‖≤M belongs to L∞. Evaluation is a continuous bilinear map from operators and vectors to vectors. Mathlib’s Hölder construction therefore sends the actual L∞ operator and an actual L² vector to an L² vector, with 1/∞+1/2=1/2. Fixing the operator gives the continuous linear map randomOperatorLp.

steps.title: Identify its representatives
steps.body: The Holder construction supplies an almost-everywhere representative identity. The representative of the L∞ equivalence class is A(ω) almost everywhere, so the constructed L² output is exactly A(ω)X(ω). This identity preserves the original probability-space coupling and permits pointwise Taylor and truncation inequalities to be applied to the actual output.

steps.title: Retain the deterministic operator bound
steps.body: Pointwise, ‖A(ω)X(ω)‖≤‖A(ω)‖‖X(ω)‖≤M‖X(ω)‖. Integrating this norm inequality gives ‖AX‖₂≤M‖X‖₂. Taking the supremum over vectors proves the operator norm of the constructed map is at most M. These estimates justify commuting the random Hessian through time integrals and bounding the integrated force correction.

KineticLangevin/LpMomentIntegral.lean.title: Fourth moments of actual time integrals
KineticLangevin/LpMomentIntegral.lean.summary: Kinetic positions are time integrals of velocities in L². A fourth-moment estimate must apply to this existing L² integral, rather than to a separately postulated L4 process. The proof uses closed convex L4 balls inside L² and the geometric fact that averages remain in a closed convex set.

steps.title: View an L4 ball inside L²
steps.body: The set lpFourthBall(R) contains actual L² equivalence classes whose extended fourth norm is at most R. If a sequence in this set converges in L², it converges in measure. Lower semicontinuity of the extended L4 norm under convergence in measure keeps its limit in the same ball. In the metric L² space, this sequential argument proves closedness.

steps.title: Verify convexity without extra moment assumptions
steps.body: For nonnegative a,b with a+b=1, the actual representative of aX+bY equals aX(ω)+bY(ω) almost everywhere. The L4 triangle inequality and homogeneity give ‖aX+bY‖₄≤a‖X‖₄+b‖Y‖₄≤R. Extended norms allow this argument even before finite fourth moments are separately established.

steps.title: Average a continuous L² path
steps.body: If every velocity v(t) on [0,T] has fourth norm at most R, its time average lies in the closed convex L4 ball. The average is T⁻¹ times the actual Bochner integral in L². Homogeneity then gives ‖∫₀ᵀv(t)dt‖₄≤TR. The zero-duration case is handled separately; for positive duration Lean checks the interval measure is finite and nonzero before applying the convex averaging theorem. This directly supplies displacement fourth moments from Gaussian velocity marginals.

KineticLangevin/FreeOU.lean.title: The free OU velocity has its actual stationary Gaussian marginal
KineticLangevin/FreeOU.lean.summary: The homogeneous OU velocity retains the actual fresh filtered Brownian innovation. Its Gaussian marginal is derived from the actual joint initial-velocity/innovation law, and its continuity and primitive are identities in the actual L² space. The later canonical source theorem proves the needed past/future joint law.

steps.title: An independent thermal innovation restores the exact standard Gaussian law
steps.body: If the initial velocity is standard Gaussian and the independent additive innovation has law \(\sqrt{1-a^2}\,\mathcal N(0,I)\), with \(a^2\le1\), their sum \(aV+N\) is exactly standard Gaussian. Lean first rewrites the true product innovation law as the pushforward of two actual independent standard Gaussian measures. It composes the addition map with that product pushforward, then applies the previously proved Gaussian linear-combination theorem using \(a^2+(\sqrt{1-a^2})^2=1\). The conclusion is an exact measure identity, rather than a covariance assumption.

steps.title: Retain the actual free OU path and its actual position primitive
steps.body: For an initial L² velocity \(V\) and the actual scaled filtered innovation path \(N_t\), define \(U_t=\psi_0(\gamma,t)V+N_t\). This is the precise free OU velocity used to combine the initial-velocity and fresh-noise Hessian correction terms. Its L² continuity follows from continuity of \(\psi_0\) and of the actual innovation path. Its exact primitive is \[\int_0^tU_s\,ds=\psi_1(\gamma,t)V+\int_0^tN_s\,ds.\] Lean splits the actual Bochner integral of the two continuous terms, moves the fixed velocity outside the scalar integral, and unfolds the defining primitive \(\psi_1\). No pointwise regularity or time-integral identity is supplied as an additional premise.

steps.title: Derive the Gaussian marginal from the actual initial/fresh-noise product law
steps.body: For \(\gamma,t\ge0\), the damping lies between zero and one, so \(\psi_0(\gamma,t)^2\le1\). Assume the actual pair \((V,N_t)\) has the explicit product law \[\mathcal N(0,I)\otimes\bigl(\sqrt{1-\psi_0(\gamma,t)^2}\,\mathcal N(0,I)\bigr).\] This premise states the actual initial/fresh-noise probability identity; canonical past/future independence proves it for the diffusion reference. Lean applies the proved Gaussian addition identity to this actual pair law. It then rewrites the almost-everywhere representatives of the L² scalar multiplication and sum, obtaining \(\operatorname{Law}(U_t)=\mathcal N(0,I)\) for the actual L² element. The result can be used in Gaussian truncation even when the initial position and velocity are dependent, since no independence from that position appears in the cutoff theorem.

KineticLangevin/LpMomentBounds.lean.title: Gaussian fourth moments control the actual Taylor error
KineticLangevin/LpMomentBounds.lean.summary: The quadratic Hessian remainder requires a fourth displacement moment, even though the stochastic solution itself lives in L². These results connect actual L4 seminorms, exact Gaussian fourth moments, and the existing L² kinematic equation.

steps.title: Turn a pointwise quadratic remainder into an L² bound
steps.body: Suppose actual random vectors D and X satisfy ‖D(ω)‖≤a‖X(ω)‖², with a≥0 and ‖X‖₄≤C. Monotonicity of the extended L² norm gives ‖D‖₂≤a‖‖X‖²‖₂. The power rule identifies the last factor with ‖X‖₄², yielding aC². Lean works first with extended nonnegative norms, where the power and monotonicity rules hold without hidden finiteness assumptions, and then converts the finite upper bound back to the actual L² norm.

steps.title: Compute the actual Gaussian L4 radius
steps.body: A standard Gaussian vector in p dimensions has fourth norm moment p²+2p. Fernique integrability ensures its fourth seminorm is finite. The integral formula for the L4 seminorm therefore yields (p²+2p)^(1/4) on any realization of the Gaussian law. This proof transfers an actual integral identity through HasLaw and keeps the 2p correction, including the one-dimensional case.

steps.title: Apply it to the existing kinetic displacement
steps.body: Assume X(t)−X(0)=∫₀ᵗV(s)ds in the actual L² space and every V(s) has the standard Gaussian marginal. Each velocity lies in the same L4 ball of radius (p²+2p)^(1/4). KineticLangevin/KernelConvolution.lean.title: Actual Wiener response convolution and all ψ time primitives
KineticLangevin/KernelConvolution.lean.summary: The φ corrections in KLMC2 are proved to be actual time convolutions of the same Brownian ψ responses. The proof establishes an ordinary integrable Fubini identity in the deterministic time-kernel Hilbert space, then applies the constructed isonormal map and spatial lift. steps.title: Name and control the ordinary causal exponential convolution
steps.body: For a continuous scalar response \(k\), define \((\mathcal E_\beta k)(t)=\int_0^t e^{-\beta(t-s)}k(s)\,ds\). Factoring the exponential gives \((\mathcal E_\beta k)(t)=e^{-\beta t}\int_0^t e^{\beta s}k(s)\,ds\). Lean proves this by the exponential addition law inside the exact interval integral. The factored form proves continuity using continuity of an ordinary primitive of a continuous function. Allowing a damping \(\beta\) distinct from the response friction \(\gamma\) makes both the φ convolution and an ordinary ψ primitive instances of the same checked theorem.

steps.title: Describe the triangular time-integration region exactly
steps.body: A Wiener response at time \(s\) has deterministic kernel \(1_{(0,s]}(r)\psi_k(\gamma,s-r)\). Integrating in \(s\in(0,t]\) therefore uses precisely the triangle \(0

steps.title: Prove the deterministic Hilbert-space Fubini identity
steps.body: Let \(K_k(t)(r)=1_{(0,t]}(r)\psi_k(\gamma,t-r)\) be the actual element of L² time. The key identity is \[K_{\mathcal E_\beta\psi_k}(t)=\int_0^t e^{-\beta(t-s)}K_k(s)\,ds.\] Lean proves equality by pairing with an arbitrary element \(f\) of this actual Hilbert space. On the finite time rectangle, \(f\) is integrable. The continuous scalar response has a finite bound on \([0,t]\), and the damping is at most one on the triangle because \(\beta\ge0\). Thus the actual double integrand is integrable, which justifies ordinary Bochner Fubini. The two triangular-domain helpers identify the two integration orders with the two sides of the claimed Hilbert identity. Commuting the continuous linear inner-product functional with the time integral completes the equality. No stochastic Fubini conclusion is assumed.

steps.title: Recover φ responses and every ψ primitive
steps.body: With \(\beta=\gamma\), the causal convolution is exactly \(\varphi_{k+1}\), so the Hilbert kernel for \(\varphi_{k+1}\) is the damped time integral of the kernel for \(\psi_k\). With \(\beta=0\), the causal convolution is the defining ordinary primitive \(\psi_{k+1}\). This gives the exact time-primitive identity for every ψ index, including the second primitive needed by the position correction. Lean specializes the already proved general Hilbert identity and rewrites the defining scalar integrals. The ordinary primitive result works for every friction, since its outer damping is zero.

steps.title: Pass the checked identities through the actual Gaussian source and spatial lift
steps.body: The actual scalar response on a Brownian interval is the constructed isonormal map applied to the translated deterministic time kernel. Translation and the isonormal map are continuous linear maps, so they commute with the actual Bochner time integrals. The proved Hilbert identities therefore yield \[N_{\varphi_{k+1}}(a,t)=\int_0^t e^{-\gamma(t-s)}N_{\psi_k}(a,s)\,ds,\qquad N_{\psi_{k+1}}(a,t)=\int_0^tN_{\psi_k}(a,s)\,ds.\] Lean proves continuity of each integrand, applies the continuous linear integral-commutation theorem, and rewrites scalar multiplication. It then applies the actual continuous linear spatial lift to obtain the same identities for arbitrary finite Euclidean coordinate sets. All responses use the very same translated Brownian source. In particular, the φ₂ and φ₃ noises in KLMC2 are exactly the damped integrals of the first and second primitives of the fresh OU noise, which is the identity required to retain the omitted stochastic Hessian-difference terms in the repaired comparison proof.

KineticLangevin/ContinuousGibbs.lean.title: The actual continuous Gibbs target and explicit exponential mixing

steps.title: Reassociate the genuine source and identify each thermal increment
steps.body: The measurable source map sends \((x,(v,B))\) to \(((v,x),B)\). Product associativity and exchange of independent position and velocity prove that this map preserves the exact phase-times-Brownian law. steps.title: Prove the complete actual initial/noise law
steps.body: Disjoint Brownian intervals give an actual iid stream of thermal Gaussian innovations. On the phase-times-Brownian product this stream is independent of the initial phase. Pulling that law back along the source reassociation and using the L² representative identities proves the full initial-phase/entire-stream product law on the actual position–velocity–noise source.

steps.title: Identify the exact stationary position law
steps.body: The selected continuous solution satisfies the genuine kinetic integral equation by construction. The actual initial/noise product law discharges every source premise of the proved splitting-limit stationarity theorem. This first proves the full actual phase has exactly the independent Gaussian-times-Gibbs target law. Projecting that phase law then gives the Gibbs position distribution at the terminal time. steps.title: Derive the full and simple explicit mixing bounds
steps.body: In the arbitrary-shift two-law theorem, start the reference position from the Gibbs distribution and use its newly proved stationarity. This produces the full explicit shifted coefficient with the true initial Wasserstein distance. For shift zero and \(m+M\le\gamma^2\), the maximum in the exponent equals \(-m\); the prefactor simplifies to \(\sqrt2\). KineticLangevin/LpHessian.lean.title: The actual frozen random Hessian and its Taylor remainder

steps.title: Freeze the true Hessian at a random position

The deterministic Hessian remainder bound is M₂‖X−Y‖²/2. If the displacement has fourth norm at most C, the quadratic-to-L² estimate gives a remainder norm at most M₂C²/2. KineticLangevin/SecondOrderLocal.lean.title: The actual cubic and quartic errors of the Hessian correction

steps.title: Build genuine damped integrals and continuous paths

The memory defect applies H₀ to the damped integral of the primitive of the damped force integral. These definitions retain the entire free-OU path, including its stochastic Hessian correction.

steps.title: Derive the local-error identity from the exact equations
steps.body: From V=U−KγG and X(s)−X(0)=∫₀ˢV, obtain ∫₀ˢU=X(s)−X(0)+∫₀ˢKγG. Substitute this identity into the correction, commute the bounded linear Hessian through the Bochner integral, and separate the frozen constant force using ∫exp(−γ(t−s))ds=ψ₁(t). Algebra then proves correctedVelocity−V equals the Taylor defect minus the memory defect. The result assumes exact mild and kinematic equations, rather than an error inequality.

steps.title: Integrate polynomial envelopes with their exact constants
steps.body: For forward time and γ≥0, the damping kernel lies in (0,1]. If ‖F(s)‖≤Csⁿ, the norm of its damped integral is at most ∫₀ᵗCsⁿds=Ctⁿ⁺¹/(n+1). The undamped case follows at γ=0. Applying this rule three times to a score bound G₀ gives the memory norm at most ‖H₀‖G₀t³/6.

steps.title: Obtain cubic velocity and quartic position errors
steps.body: A Taylor forcing bound Rs² integrates to Rt³/3. Adding the memory estimate yields velocity error at most (2R+‖H₀‖G₀)t³/6. The corrected position is X(0) plus the integral of the corrected velocity. Its difference from the exact position is therefore the integral of the actual velocity error, giving (2R+‖H₀‖G₀)t⁴/24. Continuity of the corrected velocity justifies this subtraction of integrals.

steps.title: Check the paper’s quarter-constant in transformed coordinates
steps.body: Write B=Ct³. The component estimates give ‖v‖≤B/6 and ‖x‖≤Bt/24. Under γt≤1/5, the first transformed coordinate satisfies ‖v+γx‖≤7B/40; the second has norm ‖v‖. Squaring and adding gives an energy below (B/4)², hence transformed norm at most B/4. Applying this exact component lemma with C=2R+‖H₀‖G₀ proves the actual local phase estimate. For stationary kinetic velocities and score moments, C becomes M₂√(p²+2p)+M√(Mp).

KineticLangevin/FreeOUCorrection.lean.title: The complete KLMC2 Hessian correction is an actual free-OU time integral
KineticLangevin/FreeOUCorrection.lean.summary: The fresh stochastic Hessian-difference terms are retained exactly. Their φ₂ and φ₃ responses combine with the initial velocity into the first and second time primitives of one actual free OU velocity. steps.title: Keep each deterministic and stochastic response on the same source
steps.body: Let \(L\) be the actual continuous linear pullback from the canonical Brownian L² space to the coupled probability space, including the factor \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\). Define \[R_k(t)=\psi_k(\gamma,t)V_0+L N_{\psi_k}(a,t),\qquad C_k(t)=\varphi_{k+1}(\gamma,t)V_0+L N_{\varphi_{k+1}}(a,t).\] Here every noise response uses exactly the same Brownian interval beginning at \(a\). In particular, \(R_0\) is the actual free OU velocity and \(C_1,C_2\) are the full φ₂ and φ₃ correction bundles. Lean defines these actual L² elements and proves continuity of each \(R_k\) from the checked response coefficient and canonical convolution continuity.

steps.title: Derive the exact primitive and damped-convolution identities
steps.body: The deterministic response coefficients and actual stochastic responses satisfy the same checked time-integral identities. Consequently \[R_{k+1}(t)=\int_0^tR_k(s)\,ds,\qquad C_k(t)=\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}R_k(s)\,ds.\] Lean proves integrability of every continuous summand, splits each Bochner integral, moves the fixed initial velocity outside its scalar integral, and commutes the actual source pullback with the integral. It then substitutes the proved Wiener ψ primitive or φ convolution identity. This establishes the complete correction identity, including the fresh stochastic terms absent from the displayed subtraction in the source paper.

steps.title: Pass a genuine random Hessian operator through the actual integrals
steps.body: A uniformly bounded measurable random Hessian difference acts as a proved continuous linear map \(A\) on the actual L² space. Therefore it commutes with every genuine time primitive and with the damped convolution. Lean proves this for an arbitrary actual continuous linear \(A\); the random-Hessian construction is a valid concrete instantiation. The resulting full correction identities are \[AC_1(t)=\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}\int_0^sAR_0(r)\,dr\,ds,\] and \[AC_2(t)=\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}\int_0^s\int_0^rAR_0(u)\,du\,dr\,ds.\] The proof checks continuity of every relevant L² integrand and applies the continuous linear integral-commutation theorem, then rewrites the proved primitive identities on the nonnegative integration intervals. Thus Gaussian truncation can be applied to \(AR_0(r)\) at each time, with no independence between the random Hessian and the velocity required.

steps.title: Preserve the crucial φ₂+γφ₃ cancellation for the actual noises
steps.body: The scalar response identity \(\varphi_2+\gamma\varphi_3=\psi_2\) also holds for the actual jointly sampled stochastic responses. Lean proves the corresponding equality of deterministic time-kernel L² elements by their actual almost-everywhere indicator representatives. It applies the same time translation, isonormal map, and spatial lift, all continuous and linear. This proves \[N_{\varphi_2}(a,t)+\gamma N_{\varphi_3}(a,t)=N_{\psi_2}(a,t).\] Combining this with the identical scalar coefficient relation gives the exact full-bundle identity \[C_1(t)+\gamma C_2(t)=R_2(t).\] This cancellation includes both fresh stochastic corrections. It is what permits the transformed phase estimate to use a true second primitive of the stationary free OU velocity and recover the correct quadratic time coefficient.

The spatial-lift representative theorem identifies these packed functions with the genuine vector L² segment convolutions. A countable almost-everywhere intersection handles the entire past family. Independence is unchanged by these almost-everywhere representative identities.

steps.title: Adjoin initial data and change probability sources
steps.body: Measure-preserving source composition transports independence by exact pushforward composition. For a separate independent initial coordinate, product mapping first gives the joint initial/past/future law. Product associativity then places initial data and past together opposite the future coordinate. The two product projections are independent, proving that arbitrary measurable functions of the initial data and past remain independent of the future.

steps.title: Pass independence through actual L² limits
steps.body: A continuous linear functional sends an L² vector to an L² scalar. Continuity of the actual scalar characteristic function therefore gives continuity of every dual characteristic function of the vector law. Independence is characterized by factorization of the joint dual characteristic function. For a convergent sequence of past L² variables and a fixed future variable, both the joint characteristic function and the product of marginal characteristic functions converge. Their equality at every approximation passes to the limit, proving independence of the actual limiting past variable.

steps.body: Project the actual phase pushforward law to obtain the standard Gaussian velocity marginal and the Gibbs position marginal. The Gaussian fourth moment gives the displacement Taylor forcing bound M₂√(p²+2p)t²/2. The Gibbs score theorem gives ‖∇f(X(t))‖₂≤√(Mp), while the actual frozen Hessian operator has norm at most M. KineticLangevin/FreeOUCorrectionBound.le.title: Sharp transformed Gaussian bounds for the repaired random Hessian correction
KineticLangevin/FreeOUCorrectionBound.le.summary: The actual φ₂ and φ₃ stochastic Hessian terms are estimated together. Their exact ψ₂ cancellation gives the sharp quadratic time coefficient. Gaussian truncation then supplies the source-paper random-Hessian contribution without discarding fresh-noise terms or assuming independence from the Hessian.

steps.title: Prove the sharp first and second primitive estimates
steps.body: If \(\|U_r\|\le C\) on \([0,t]\), then \(\|\int_0^sU_r\,dr\|\le Cs\). Integrating this genuine bound yields \[\left\|\int_0^t\int_0^sU_r\,dr\,ds\right\|\le\frac{Ct^2}{2}.\] The same estimate holds with the outer factor \(e^{-\gamma(t-s)}\) for \(\gamma\ge0\), since that scalar lies between zero and one. The exact scalar primitive gives the factor \(1/2\). Every interval endpoint and nonnegative damping condition is checked explicitly.

steps.title: Use the full stochastic cancellation in the actual phase metric
steps.body: Let \(A\) be the actual continuous linear random-Hessian operator and suppose \(\|AR_0(r)\|_{L^2}\le C\). The transformed phase norm combines exactly these two coordinates, hence \[\|T_{\gamma,0}(AC_1,AC_2)\|\le\frac{\sqrt2}{2}t^2C.\] Lean rewrites the two actual primitive identities, applies the two sharp integral bounds, commutes \(A\) with the exact correction balance, and sums the two squared component bounds. It finally checks the square of the displayed nonnegative bound. This controls the entire implemented correction.

steps.title: Insert the actual Gaussian cutoff at each free-OU time
steps.body: If every actual free-OU velocity marginal is standard Gaussian and \(\|AR_0(r)(\omega)\|\le\min\{B,M_2\|X(\omega)\|\}\|R_0(r)(\omega)\|\), the proved truncation theorem gives the same bound at every time: \[\|AR_0(r)\|_{L^2}\le M_2\sqrt\alpha\,\|X\|_{L^2}+2B e^{-(\alpha-p)/8},\qquad\alpha\ge5p.\] Substituting this common \(C\) in the sharp transformed estimate retains both terms with their exact constants. Lean constructs the nonnegative common bound and applies the actual Gaussian truncation theorem at each time. No independence between the Hessian factor, the position discrepancy, and the velocity is required.

steps.title: Verify the cutoff premise for a concrete random operator
steps.body: For an actual measurable random operator field \(H(\omega)\), suppose its true operator norm satisfies both \(\|H(\omega)\|\le B\) and \(\|H(\omega)\|\le M_2\|X(\omega)\|\) almost everywhere. The checked random-operator construction gives an actual L² continuous linear map with representative \(H(\omega)V(\omega)\). Thus the required cutoff estimate follows from the genuine uniform and Lipschitz operator bounds of a Hessian difference.

steps.body: The coupling extension has independent Gaussian velocity and a canonical Brownian coordinate. The proved Brownian support theorem makes this whole stream independent of the future response. Adjoin the independent initial positions and velocity, and reassociate the actual product source. The future marginal itself is exactly the translated OU thermal Gaussian law, by the proved Brownian convolution distribution and measure-preserving source projection.

Combining this marginal, the exact future thermal Gaussian marginal and the newly proved independence gives their full product joint law. KineticLangevin/SecondOrderLinear.lean.title: The genuine frozen-linear contraction in Proposition 3
KineticLangevin/SecondOrderLinear.lean.summary: The friction can be much larger than the square root of the smoothness constant. A crude Euler remainder proportional to γ² would lose the paper’s step-size regime. The identities below instead use the force’s cocoercivity to retain a second-order budget proportional to M, and prove the actual frozen-linear map contracts by 1−mt/(2γ) under 5γMt≤m.

steps.title: Separate fast damping from the Euler remainder
steps.body: For the kinetic difference drift A=(−γv−F,v), its transformed squared norm satisfies the exact identity E(A)=−γE′/2+2‖F‖²−γ²⟨x,F⟩. The actual Euler phase (v,x)+sA has energy E+sE′+s²E(A). steps.title: Use cocoercivity before bounding the remainder
steps.body: The force satisfies ‖F‖²≤M⟨x,F⟩ and ⟨x,F⟩≤M‖x‖². Since γ²≥m+M, 2M−γ²≤M−m. Also γ²‖x‖²≤2E. Combining these facts gives E(A)≤−γE′/2+2M(M−m)E/γ². In the Euler expansion, the derivative coefficient becomes s(1−γs/2), which is nonnegative for γs≤1. Actual force dissipativity E′≤−2mE/γ then yields transformed norm at most [1−ms/γ+(m/2+M(M−m)/γ²)s²] times the initial norm. The final square comparison retains an additional nonnegative square instead of estimating it away.

steps.title: Bound the true frozen-Hessian correction
steps.body: The remaining phase correction is (−φ₂Hv,−ψ₂F−φ₃Hv). The exact coefficient identity φ₂+γφ₃=ψ₂ transforms it into (−ψ₂(Hv+γF),φ₂Hv). The bounds ψ₂,φ₂≤t²/2, ‖H‖≤M, ‖v‖≤N, and γ‖x‖≤3N/2 give component envelopes 5Mt²N/4 and Mt²N/2. Their squared sum is below (3Mt²N/2)². Thus the actual correction costs at most 3Mt²N/2, with no symmetry or common Hessian eigenbasis assumed.

steps.title: Check the scalar coefficient budget with exact ψ₁
steps.body: The friction balance γψ₂=t−ψ₁ and ψ₂≤t²/2 imply ψ₁≥t−γt²/2, while 0≤ψ₁≤t. Moreover m+M(M−m)/γ²≤M. These inequalities bound the Euler coefficient plus the frozen correction by 1−mt/γ+5Mt²/2. The source step restriction 5γMt≤m makes the last term at most mt/(2γ), leaving 1−mt/(2γ). All divisions are justified by positive friction.

steps.title: Identify and contract the actual frozen-linear map
steps.body: frozenSecondOrderStep is the explicit phase with ψ₀v−ψ₁F−φ₂Hv in velocity and x+ψ₁v−ψ₂F−φ₃Hv in position. The identity ψ₀=1−γψ₁ writes this actual map as the Euler phase plus the correction above. Strong-smooth interpolation supplies both cocoercivity and force dissipativity. The transformed triangle inequality and the checked scalar budget therefore prove the source contraction factor for the actual frozen-linear part of KLMC2.

KineticLangevin/HessianDifference.lean.title: The genuine sharp Hessian-difference bound and its Gaussian L² cutoff
KineticLangevin/HessianDifference.lean.summary: The actual Hessians of one strongly convex smooth potential differ in operator norm by at most M−m. The proof derives this directly from the checked centered gradient sector inequality and genuine derivatives. It then proves the identical bound for the actual random L² Hessian operators and establishes the precise Gaussian truncation term used in the repaired KLMC2 comparison.

steps.title: Center the gradient and derive its sharp Lipschitz radius
steps.body: For an \(m\)-strongly convex potential with \(M\)-Lipschitz gradient, the checked strong-smooth interpolation inequality implies \[\left\| abla f(x)- abla f(y)- rac{m+M}{2}(x-y) ight\|\le rac{M-m}{2}\|x-y\|.\] Thus \(g_c(x)= abla f(x)- rac{m+M}{2}x\) is globally \((M-m)/2\)-Lipschitz. Lean constructs the nonnegative Lipschitz constant, rewrites the difference of the centered gradients as the residual in this previously proved sector estimate, and applies that exact estimate. No Hessian or spectral conclusion is inserted as a premise.

steps.title: Derive the actual Hessian curvature-width bound from actual derivatives
steps.body: If \(H_x=D\nabla f(x)\), the genuine derivative of the centered gradient is \(H_x-\frac{m+M}{2}I\). The derivative of a globally Lipschitz map has operator norm at most its Lipschitz constant, so \[\left\|H_x-\frac{m+M}{2}I\right\|\le\frac{M-m}{2}.\] Lean differentiates the actual centered gradient by subtracting the scalar identity derivative, then applies the checked derivative/Lipschitz operator bound. Subtracting the centered derivatives at two actual points yields \[\|H_x-H_y\|\le\frac{M-m}{2}+\frac{M-m}{2}=M-m.\] This is the sharp Hessian interval-width estimate. It is derived from the original potential assumptions and actual gradient derivatives, without an additional continuous-Hessian, symmetry, or operator-range hypothesis.

steps.title: Identify and bound the actual random Hessian difference on L²
steps.body: The existing random-Hessian construction is an actual continuous linear map on L², with representative \(H(X(\omega))Z(\omega)\). Lean proves that subtracting the two such maps has the exact representative \[(H(X(\omega))-H(Y(\omega)))Z(\omega).\] It rewrites the actual almost-everywhere representatives of the two random Hessians and their L² difference. The pointwise sharp bound just proved gives \(\|(H(X)-H(Y))Z\|\le(M-m)\|Z\|\), so the true L² operator norm of the difference is at most \(M-m\). Lean applies the actual L² norm monotonicity theorem and the continuous linear operator-norm characterization; no operator bound is assumed on an unspecified random map.

steps.title: Prove the exact Hessian-difference Gaussian truncation term
steps.body: The original Hessian Lipschitz assumption also gives \(\|H(X)-H(Y)\|\le M_2\|X-Y\|\) pointwise. Combining this with the genuine uniform bound \(M-m\), and retaining an actual standard Gaussian velocity \(V\), gives \[\|(H(X)-H(Y))V\|_{L^2}\le M_2\sqrt\alpha\,\|X-Y\|_{L^2}+2(M-m)e^{-(\alpha-p)/8},\qquad\alpha\ge5p.\] Lean rewrites the exact random-Hessian difference representative and the actual position discrepancy representative, combines the two proved operator bounds by their minimum, and applies the checked Gaussian cutoff theorem. Only the actual marginal Gaussian law of \(V\) is required; the positions and Hessian difference may depend on \(V\). This is the precise random coefficient bound needed at each free-OU time in the corrected KLMC2 argument.

KineticLangevin/MassScaling.lean.title: Normalize inverse mass in the actual kinetic equation
KineticLangevin/MassScaling.lean.summary: The manuscript’s Lemma 1 removes inverse mass \(u>0\) by setting \(c=\sqrt u\), changing time to \(t/c\), and dividing velocity by \(c\). This proof works with the complete integral equation in an arbitrary complete normed space, so it applies to the constructed L² Brownian solution without differentiating its noise.

steps.title: Normalize the true phase drift
steps.body: The continuous linear map \(D_a(v,x)=(av,x)\) changes velocity alone. Expanding both components proves \(c^{-1}D_{c^{-1}}R_{g,\gamma,c^2}(z)=R_{g,\gamma/c,1}(D_{c^{-1}}z)\). In the first component, the time and velocity factors cancel the original \(c^2\) force factor. In the second, the transformed position derivative is the normalized velocity. Lean verifies these as vector equalities using scalar action identities.

steps.title: Transform the integral and its actual Brownian amplitude
steps.body: Apply the bounded linear map to the solution identity at \(t/c\), pass it through the Bochner integral, and substitute \(r=s/c\). The transformed equation has friction \(\gamma/c\) and inverse mass one. The additive input becomes \(c^{-1}B_{t/c}\). For the original thermal amplitude \(\sqrt{2\gamma c^2}\), the coefficient identity gives \(c^{-1}\sqrt{2\gamma c^2}=\sqrt{2\gamma/c}\sqrt c\). The separately proved changed-clock Brownian process is \(\sqrt c W_{t/c}\), so the resulting equation has exactly the required fluctuation-dissipation coefficient. Positivity of \(c\) supplies both the interval inclusion and the square-root cancellations.

KineticLangevin/Accuracy.lean.title: An explicit epsilon guarantee for the actual KLMC sampler
KineticLangevin/Accuracy.lean.summary: The convergence theorem becomes an executable mathematical budget: choose a positive step, an integer iteration count, and obtain a certified error at most \(\varepsilon\). The result concerns the actual constructed sampler. Neither a recurrence nor a local-error estimate is left as a premise.

steps.title: Verify that the geometric factor is admissible
steps.body: Set \(\alpha=3mh/(4\gamma)\). The curvature, friction and step assumptions imply \(0<\alpha\le1\). The proof reuses the checked exponential-coefficient estimate: \(e^{-mh/\gamma}+(3/4)Mh^2\le1-\alpha\). Its left side is positive, so the right side is nonnegative. This justifies every later geometric and logarithmic estimate.

steps.title: Apply the scalar error allocation to the actual law
steps.body: The actual KLMC theorem gives \(W_2(\nu_n,\pi)\le\sqrt2(1-\alpha)^nD+b\). The checked scalar budget allocates \(b\le0.94\varepsilon\) and \((1-\alpha)^nD\le\varepsilon/24\). The sum is at most \(\varepsilon\). The threshold is the natural ceiling of \(\max\{0,\log(24D/\varepsilon)/\alpha\}\); if \(D=0\), no initial-error iterations are needed. The finite-transport hypothesis prevents the real-valued Wasserstein convention from hiding an infinite distance.

steps.title: Choose the paper step and round the count
steps.body: For positive dimension choose \(h=\min\{m/(4\gamma M),\,0.94\varepsilon m/(M\sqrt{2p})\}\). Both terms are positive. The first enforces stability and the second enforces the bias budget by multiplication through positive denominators. Construct the corresponding nonnegative-real Lean step, use the rounded logarithmic count, and apply the actual accuracy theorem. At \(\gamma=\sqrt{m+M}\), this is precisely the manuscript’s minimum-step prescription. The explicit reciprocal dependence displays the \(\sqrt p/\varepsilon\) iteration scaling up to the logarithm.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalKLMC2Noise.lean.title: The actual four-kernel correlated Gaussian KLMC2 noise

Their correlations are essential. This module constructs those four responses simultaneously in every spatial coordinate, proves their exact Gram Gaussian law and iid time stream, and lifts the same random variables to arbitrary initial coupling extensions.

steps.body: The Euclidean space uses an arbitrary finite spatial coordinate set. Packing transposes the array of scalar four-dimensional blocks into four full spatial vectors. Pushing the product of the actual four-dimensional Gram Gaussians through this pack map defines the exact vector innovation law, which is a probability measure.

steps.body: Apply all four deterministic kernels to the same Brownian interval and pack all independent spatial copies. Brownian intervals have disjoint supports, so these full correlated vectors are independent across time. At each step their law is the packed product of the exact scalar Gram Gaussian laws. The independent-family product-law theorem therefore proves the complete implemented stream has the actual iid Gaussian distribution.

steps.body: The four L² innovations are directly the vector Brownian convolutions, so no separate Gaussian realization is substituted. Their representative theorem identifies every coordinate with the corresponding implemented packed response on the same source. Finite second moments follow from the L² construction and this exact almost-everywhere identity.

A countable almost-everywhere intersection identifies the entire lifted stream with the original stream, and source projection preserves its exact iid law.

steps.body: Scalar multiplication, subtraction and addition of L² classes agree with the corresponding operations on their representatives almost everywhere. steps.body: The lifted gradient has the original gradient as its representative. Substitution in the two affine coordinates identifies the complete L² step with the actual vector KLMC2 formula. steps.body: Continuity of the original force and Hessian makes the full state-and-four-noise update measurable. Its deterministic recursion equals the general random recursion with the same update.
