KineticLangevin/CorrectedStep.lean.title: The implemented KLMC2 step is the genuine corrected free-OU path
KineticLangevin/CorrectedStep.lean.summary: The local Taylor estimate and the actual four-noise numerical map refer to exactly the same L² random variables. This module proves the identification, including both stochastic Hessian corrections, by genuine time differentiation and integration.

steps.title: Differentiate the true damped convolution
steps.body: For a continuous Banach-valued path \(F\), write \(D_\gamma F(t)=\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}F(s)\,ds\). Factoring the exponential yields \(D_\gamma F(t)=e^{-\gamma t}\int_0^te^{\gamma s}F(s)\,ds\). Lean applies the fundamental theorem of calculus to the continuous integrand and the product rule, then cancels \(e^{-\gamma t}e^{\gamma t}=1\). The result is the exact equation \((D_\gamma F)\prime=F-\gamma D_\gamma F\), for every real time.

steps.title: Integrate the entire stochastic correction
steps.body: The actual canonical Wiener kernel on an interval of zero duration is zero in L²; Lean proves this by almost-everywhere equality of its deterministic kernel, then applies the isonormal map and spatial lift. Thus the full correction \(C_k(t)=\varphi_{k+1}(t)V_0+L N_{\varphi_{k+1}}(a,t)\) vanishes initially and is continuous. The checked identity \(C_1+\gamma C_2=R_2\), together with \(C_2=D_\gamma R_2\), gives \(C_2\prime=C_1\) at every positive time. The fundamental theorem then proves \(C_2(t)=\int_0^tC_1(s)\,ds\). Also \(C_1=D_\gamma(\int_0^{\cdot}R_0)\), using the genuine primitive \(R_1=\int R_0\). Both statements include fresh noise terms.

steps.title: Identify the analytic velocity and position with full kernel formulas
steps.body: The Taylor analysis defines \(\widehat V_t=R_0(t)-\psi_1(t)F_0-A D_\gamma(\int R_0)(t)\). Substituting the proved identity gives \(\widehat V_t=R_0(t)-\psi_1(t)F_0-AC_1(t)\). Integrating this true path gives \(\widehat X_t=x_0+R_1(t)-\psi_2(t)F_0-AC_2(t)\). Lean first proves equality of the velocity integrands on the actual time interval, establishes all continuous summands are integrable, splits their Bochner integrals, and commutes the bounded Hessian operator with the integral. It then uses the checked primitive identities and additive algebra.

steps.title: Match the implemented four-noise KLMC2 update exactly
steps.body: Let \(R\) be the unscaled source pullback and sample the four correlated responses \((N_{\psi_0},N_{\psi_1},N_{\varphi_2},N_{\varphi_3})\) on the same Brownian interval. The analytic free-OU path uses the thermally scaled map \(L=\sqrt{2\gamma}\,R\). Expanding the proved velocity and position formulas gives precisely the implemented \(\texttt{klmc2Step}\): its deterministic Hessian terms are \(-\varphi_2H_0V_0\) and \(-\varphi_3H_0V_0\), and its fresh terms are \(\sqrt{2\gamma}(N_{\psi_0}-H_0N_{\varphi_2})\) and \(\sqrt{2\gamma}(N_{\psi_1}-H_0N_{\varphi_3})\). Lean reduces the four finite indices, applies linearity of the actual Hessian and source maps, and closes the two component identities by module algebra. No local error or noise-independence conclusion is assumed.

KineticLangevin/KLMC2ProductLaw.lean.title: One actual KLMC2 output law for every initial coupling

Its terminal position defines the output map and its product-source pushforward defines the actual law. The force and Hessian are continuous, so the complete four-noise step is measurable. Induction over the original recursion proves the output map is almost everywhere measurable from the square-integrable source data.

steps.body: The pointwise correspondence theorem for the genuine random-Hessian L² chain identifies every iterate with the original vector recursion. The initial velocity, initial coupling coordinate and all countably many four-noise values have exactly their source representatives. Substituting these identities proves the L² output equals the original fixed-source output map composed with the initial/source projection. That projection has exactly the independent initial-position/source product law. Pushforward composition therefore proves the actual output law is independent of the chosen transport coupling. Its measurability also confirms it is a probability measure.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalFreeOU.lean.title: The actual fresh free-OU velocity has its Gaussian marginal
KineticLangevin/CanonicalFreeOU.lean.summary: The Gaussian cutoff in the repaired second-order proof applies to a true free-OU path on each actual reference interval. Its marginal law follows from proved stationarity and proved independence of future Brownian increments from the actual past solution.

steps.title: Use the actual reference-grid joint law
steps.body: At the grid time \(a=nh\), let \(V_a\) be the velocity of the actual stationary reference chain and let \(N_{\psi_0}(a,r)\) be its actual fresh Brownian response. The checked past/future theorem gives the joint law \[\bigl(V_a,\sqrt{2\gamma}N_{\psi_0}(a,r)\bigr)\sim N(0,I)\otimes N\bigl(0,(1-e^{-2\gamma r})I\bigr).\] In particular, the first random variable is independent of this future response even though it depends on the entire past path. Lean specializes this exact joint law to the nonnegative real duration, then applies the proved Gaussian addition identity to \(R_0(r)=e^{-\gamma r}V_a+\sqrt{2\gamma}N_{\psi_0}(a,r)\). Its covariance is \(e^{-2\gamma r}I+(1-e^{-2\gamma r})I=I\), so \(R_0(r)\sim N(0,I)\). All variables are the actual L² representatives used by the numerical coupling.

steps.title: Apply the same result at arbitrary continuous reference times
steps.body: The global reference solution has the same proven past/future joint law at every \(a\in[0,T]\). The identical Gaussian calculation therefore proves the free-OU response beginning at an arbitrary continuous reference time is standard Gaussian at every later duration. This supports local cutoff estimates independently of a chosen numerical grid. Neither statement assumes the desired marginal or an adaptedness contract; both invoke the already proved canonical independence and stationarity results.

KineticLangevin/ScalarConvolution.lean.title: Every scalar convolution identity in the source lemma
KineticLangevin/ScalarConvolution.lean.summary: The two general coefficient identities are proved for every pair of natural indices. The primitive identity starts at φ₁, as required by the definition φ₀=0; the convolution identity includes both zero indices. The proofs hold for every real friction and time.

steps.title: Move a primitive between the two convolution factors
steps.body: Differentiate \(\psi_{k+1}(s)\psi_{j+1}(t-s)\). Its derivative is \(\psi_k(s)\psi_{j+1}(t-s)-\psi_{k+1}(s)\psi_j(t-s)\). Both boundary products vanish because every positive-index response vanishes at zero. Lean proves the derivative by the product and chain rules, proves both continuous terms integrable, and applies the fundamental theorem. Therefore \[\int_0^t\psi_k(s)\psi_{j+1}(t-s)\,ds=\int_0^t\psi_{k+1}(s)\psi_j(t-s)\,ds.\] Induction moves the entire second index to the first. At second index zero the defining exponential convolution gives exactly \(\varphi_{k+1}\), proving \(\varphi_{k+j+1}=\psi_k*\psi_j\) for all \(k,j\ge0\).

steps.title: Derive the full friction recurrence
steps.body: Use the just-proved identity with \(j=1\), multiply the integral by \(\gamma\), and substitute \(\gamma\psi_1(t-s)=1-\psi_0(t-s)\). Splitting the genuine scalar integral yields \[\varphi_{k+1}(t)+\gamma\varphi_{k+2}(t)=\psi_{k+1}(t).\] Lean establishes continuity and integrability before splitting; no division by friction is needed. The recurrence therefore includes \(\gamma=0\).

steps.title: Differentiate and integrate the actual correction coefficients
steps.body: The factored definition \(\varphi_{k+1}(t)=e^{-\gamma t}\int_0^te^{\gamma s}\psi_k(s)\,ds\) has derivative \(\psi_k(t)-\gamma\varphi_{k+1}(t)\). Lean applies the fundamental theorem, product rule, and exact exponential cancellation. At the next index the friction recurrence reduces this derivative to \(\varphi_{k+1}(t)\). Since the next correction vanishes at zero, integrating gives \[\varphi_{k+2}(t)=\int_0^t\varphi_{k+1}(s)\,ds.\] This is the first source identity with its necessary index restriction: the printed assertion at \(k=0\) would incorrectly equate positive \(\varphi_1(t)=te^{-\gamma t}\) with the integral of \(\varphi_0=0\).

KineticLangevin/SecondOrderRecurrence.le.title: Absorb the Hessian cutoff and accumulate the second-order error
KineticLangevin/SecondOrderRecurrence.le.summary: The repaired local comparison has a random-Hessian term proportional to \(M_2\sqrt\alpha h^2\). Choosing the cutoff \(\alpha=(m/(4M_2h))^2\) absorbs it into the contraction gap. This module proves the choice, both Gaussian tails, the affine accumulation, the position projection, and the exact dimension range for the manuscript’s final simplification.

steps.title: Choose the cutoff and retain both tail estimates
steps.body: For \(m,M_2,h>0\), the positive square root of \(\alpha=(m/(4M_2h))^2\) is \(m/(4M_2h)\). Thus \(M_2\sqrt\alpha h=m/4\). The source dimension restriction \(4\sqrt{5p}M_2h\le m\) implies \(\alpha\ge5p\). It follows that \((\alpha-p)/8\ge p/2\), giving the printed tail. Also \(p\le\alpha/5\) implies \((\alpha-p)/8\ge\alpha/10=m^2/(160M_2^2h^2)\), giving the stronger source footnote. Lean proves the square-root identity, multiplies through positive denominators, compares nonnegative squares, and applies monotonicity of the exponential.

steps.title: Sum the actual one-step comparison and project to position
steps.body: The local bound has coefficient \(1-mh/(2\gamma)+M_2\sqrt\alpha h^2/\gamma\). The cutoff makes this at most \(q=1-mh/(4\gamma)\). The additive local terms are \(\sqrt2h^2B e^{-(\alpha-p)/8}+h^3C/4\), where \(B=M-m\) and \(C=M_2\sqrt{p^2+2p}+M\sqrt{Mp}\). The checked affine recurrence divides this budget by \(1-q=mh/(4\gamma)\). Position projection multiplies by \(\sqrt2/\gamma\), and equal initial velocities give \(e_0\le\gamma d_0\). The exact resulting bias is \(\sqrt2h^2C/m+(8B/m)h e^{-(\alpha-p)/8}\), with the desired transient \(\sqrt2q^nd_0\). The recurrence is a reusable scalar lemma; the actual chain endpoint supplies its one-step inequality separately.

steps.title: State the dimension restriction explicitly
steps.body: For \(p\ge2\), \(p^2+2p\le2p^2\), hence \(\sqrt2\sqrt{p^2+2p}\le2p\). Distributing this through \(C\) gives the printed Hessian term \(2M_2p\), while \(\sqrt2\sqrt{Mp}=\sqrt{2Mp}\) gives the score term. The supplied proof’s simplification does not justify the same expression at \(p=1\). The general theorem therefore retains the exact fourth-moment expression there; the printed simplification is an explicit \(p\ge2\) corollary. Lean compares nonnegative squares and never uses the invalid inequality in dimension one.

KineticLangevin/CanonicalKLMC2Law.lean.title: The genuine canonical KLMC2 Gaussian Markov law and coupling bridge
KineticLangevin/CanonicalKLMC2Law.lean.summary: The second-order sampler is now a single actual Gaussian Markov law, not a law depending on an analysis coupling. The zero and successor identities expose the genuine initial state and recurrence needed by the stochastic convergence proof.

Existence of a finite-cost initial plan therefore proves the true output Wasserstein distance is finite. KineticLangevin/SecondOrderComparison.le.title: Proposition 3 with the full stochastic Hessian difference

With the lift scaled by sqrt(2 gamma), direct linear algebra proves this is exactly Integrator.klmc2Step at the unscaled four-kernel innovations. Freeze the linear part at the Hessian of the second starting position; its data are the actual velocity, position and force differences. The remainder is minus the Hessian difference applied to the complete phi2 and phi3 free-OU corrections built from the first reference velocity. steps.title: Supply the frozen-linear estimate from the actual potential
steps.body: The actual L2 gradient retains its Lipschitz constant and centered strong-smooth sector. The actual random Hessian has operator norm at most M. The frozen-linear map therefore contracts by 1-mt/(2 gamma) under gamma^2 at least m+M and 5 gamma M t at most m. The checked deterministic theorem is applied in the Hilbert space of actual square-integrable random vectors.

steps.title: Combine the actual coupled terms by Minkowski
steps.body: The generic triangle lemma applies the exact difference identity, invariance of transformed norm under negation, and the Euclidean phase triangle inequality. Its two inputs are the separately proved frozen-linear component and the complete Hessian correction. This elementary composition introduces no stochastic approximation or omitted noise.

steps.title: Prove the repaired source comparison inequality
steps.body: Let A be the difference of the two actual random Hessian operators. Each actual free-OU velocity is standard Gaussian. The genuine Hessian difference bound M-m and Hessian Lipschitz constant M2 give the cutoff norm M2 sqrt(alpha) times the L2 position difference plus 2(M-m)exp(-(alpha-p)/8), for alpha at least 5p. Combining this with frozen-linear contraction and position projection proves transformed error at most [1-mt/(2 gamma)+M2 sqrt(alpha)t^2/gamma] times the initial transformed error, plus sqrt(2)t^2(M-m)exp(-(alpha-p)/8). The Gaussian premise is an actual source law and is discharged by the canonical past/future construction.

KineticLangevin/SecondOrderOneStep.lean.title: The actual second-order one-step coupling recurrence
KineticLangevin/SecondOrderOneStep.lean.summary: These results connect the implemented four-kernel KLMC2 update to the true stationary kinetic segment and combine the genuine local and repaired comparison estimates. steps.title: Combine local defect and repaired synchronous comparison
steps.body: Insert the numerical update starting at the stationary reference into the difference between the actual numerical update and exact reference endpoint. steps.title: Derive both derivatives along every actual affine line

steps.title: Choose the exact source minimum at normalized precision
steps.body: Let \(A=2M_2p+M\sqrt{2Mp}\). The two printed quadratic terms add to \(A h^2/m\). steps.body: Immediately before introducing its refined condition-number shorthand, the manuscript writes the work scale as \(\sqrt M/(m h_\varepsilon)\). steps.body: Set \(\kappa=M/m\), \(\eta=M_2/(m\sqrt m)\), and choose the least admissible source friction \(\gamma=\sqrt{m+M}\). The exact normalization is \[\frac{4\sqrt{m+M}}{m}\,Q=\operatorname{Work}(\kappa,\eta,p,\varepsilon),\] where secondOrderNormalizedWork is the concrete maximum analyzed in the condition-number chapter. steps.title: Round logarithmic time to an actual integer count
steps.body: The existing iteration count is \(N(\alpha,D,\delta)=\lceil\max(0,\log(24D/\delta)/\alpha)\rceil\), with a natural-number ceiling. For \(\alpha>0\), division commutes with the maximum against zero. The ceiling inequality therefore gives \[N(\alpha,D,\delta)<1+\frac{\max\{0,\log(24D/\delta)\}}{\alpha}.\] The maximum is essential when the initial discrepancy is already small; it prevents a negative logarithmic threshold from being interpreted as a negative iteration count. Substitute \(\alpha=mh_0/(4\gamma)\), \(\delta=\varepsilon/\sqrt m\), and \(h_0^{-1}=Q\) to obtain the exact bound \[N\!\left(\frac{mh_0}{4\gamma},D,\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt m}\right)<1+\frac{4\gamma}{m}\,Q\,\max\!\left\{0,\log\frac{24D\sqrt m}{\varepsilon}\right\}.\] Lean explicitly rewrites the normalized logarithm argument, applies the positive-rate ceiling estimate, and uses the proved reciprocal identity. In an application \(D\) is the initial Wasserstein discrepancy. This scalar upper bound does not discard any term from the separate full-tail sampler theorem.

steps.title: Check the friction choice directly
steps.body: At fixed positive step and nonnegative initial error, increasing positive friction decreases \(mh/(4\gamma)\), hence increases the geometric factor \((1-mh/(4\gamma))^n\). Lean proves the reciprocal inequality for the two friction values, uses the lower-friction stability condition to keep the base nonnegative, and applies monotonicity of a natural power. This proves the two concrete monotonicity statements behind the manuscript's choice of the least permitted \(\gamma\).

steps.title: Bound the actual rounded count by the corrected physical condition numbers
steps.body: The final corollary applies to the very natural-number count selected by the explicit step \(h_0\), with \(\gamma=\sqrt{m+M}\). Assume \(m>0\), \(m\le M\), \(M_2>0\), \(p\ge1\), and \(\varepsilon>0\). Write \(\kappa=M/m\), \(\kappa_2=(M_2^{2/3}+Mp^{-1/3})/m\), and \(R=\max(\kappa,\kappa_2)\). The proved integer-count bound becomes \[N\!\left(\frac{mh_0}{4\sqrt{m+M}},D,\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt m}\right)<1+64\left[\sqrt p\,R^2+\sqrt{p/\varepsilon}\,R^{5/4}\right]\max\!\left\{0,\log\frac{24D\sqrt m}{\varepsilon}\right\}.\] Lean first uses the exact ceiling-count theorem. It rewrites the work prefactor through the normalization identity, then invokes secondOrderNormalizedWork_physical_bound, whose hypotheses follow from these physical parameters. Multiplication by the nonnegative maximum-logarithm preserves that upper bound. This assembles the explicit step, the rounded integer count, and the corrected condition-number refinement into one theorem; it does not assume a comparison between the two condition numbers.

KineticLangevin/ConditionNumber.lean.title: Correcting the Hessian condition-number refinement
KineticLangevin/ConditionNumber.lean.summary: The supplied manuscript informally simplifies its tail-free KLMC2 step/count budget using \(\kappa_2=(M_2^{2/3}+Mp^{-1/3})/m\). This module proves a valid refinement with \(\max(\kappa,\kappa_2)\), identifies the extra regime in which the printed shape follows, and constructs an exact natural-dimension family disproving a uniform removal of the ordinary condition number. Every scalar quantity is tied to the actual source definition. These are statements about the explicit budget prescription, with its Gaussian tail intentionally excluded; the separate actual-sampler accuracy theorems include that tail.

steps.title: Keep both condition numbers and normalize the actual source definition
steps.body: The ordinary gradient condition number is \(\kappa=M/m\). The supplied source proposes \(\rho=(M_2^{2/3}+Mp^{-1/3})/m\). Introduce the dimensionless Hessian ratio \(\eta=M_2/(m\sqrt m)\). The first proof establishes the exact identity \(\rho=\eta^{2/3}+\kappa p^{-1/3}\), rather than assuming a convenient relationship between the two quantities. Positivity of \(m\) permits the real-power product and quotient rules: \((m\sqrt m)^{2/3}=m\). Lean rewrites the square root as a half power, combines exponents, distributes the quotient power, and closes the remaining fraction identity with ring.

steps.title: Derive the useful cubic inequalities from the definition
steps.body: For \(\kappa>0\), \(\eta\ge0\), and \(p>0\), the source quantity \(\rho\) is positive. Each nonnegative summand is at most their sum. Cubing \(\eta^{2/3}\le\rho\) gives \(\eta^2\le\rho^3\). Cubing \(\kappa p^{-1/3}\le\rho\), and using \((p^{-1/3})^3=1/p\), gives \(\kappa^3\le p\rho^3\). These estimates justify the later dimension scaling; they do not imply \(\kappa\le\rho\). The proof uses monotonicity of natural powers on nonnegative numbers, then multiplies through the positive dimension.

steps.title: Record the exact reciprocal-step coefficient before simplifying it
steps.body:
Choose \(\gamma=\sqrt{m+M}\), put \(s=h\sqrt m\), and target error \(\varepsilon/\sqrt m\). The two stability restrictions and the source quadratic-bias allocation give

\[s^{-1}=\max\left\{5\kappa\sqrt{1+\kappa},\ 4\sqrt{5p}\eta,\ \sqrt{\frac{4\eta p+2\sqrt2\kappa\sqrt\kappa\sqrt p}{\varepsilon}}\right\}.\]

The transient count has coefficient \(4\sqrt{1+\kappa}/s\), before its logarithm and integer rounding. secondOrderNormalizedWork keeps this entire expression, including the constants. The separate secondOrderRefinement records the source's proposed shape \(\sqrt p\rho^2+\sqrt{p/\varepsilon}\rho^{5/4}\). This section concerns the source's expressly tail-free comparison; the actual sampler's separate epsilon theorem controls the Gaussian tail as well.

steps.title: Bound the three branches with one explicit universal constant
steps.body:
Suppose \(1\le\kappa\le R\), \(p\ge1\), and \(\eta^2\le R^3\). Comparing nonnegative squares gives \(\eta\le R\sqrt R\), while \(\sqrt p\le p\) and \(\kappa\sqrt\kappa\le R\sqrt R\). Thus the numerator of the accuracy branch is at most \(8pR\sqrt R\). Let \(A=\sqrt pR^2\) and \(B=\sqrt{p/\varepsilon}R^{5/4}\). Their exact squares are \(A^2=pR^4\) and \(B^2=(p/\varepsilon)R^2\sqrt R\).

After multiplying by the common count factor, the ordinary stability branch is at most \(40A\). The Hessian stability branch has squared value \(1280p(1+\kappa)\eta^2\le2560pR^4\le(64A)^2\). The accuracy branch has square at most \(256(p/\varepsilon)R^2\sqrt R=(16B)^2\). All quantities are nonnegative, so the square comparisons recover the original inequalities. Taking their maximum gives the checked bound \(64(A+B)\). The Lean proof expands these squares, applies order-preserving multiplication, and uses the real-power identity \((R^{5/4})^2=R^2\sqrt R\).

steps.title: Apply the bound to the source parameters without adding a false comparison
steps.body:
Set \(R=\max\{\kappa,\rho\}\), where \(\rho\) is the actual source quantity. Then \(R\ge\kappa\), and the proved cubic estimate gives \(\eta^2\le\rho^3\le R^3\). The previous theorem therefore yields

\[\mathcal W(\kappa,\eta,p,\varepsilon)\le64\left[\sqrt p\,\max(\kappa,\rho)^2+\sqrt{p/\varepsilon}\,\max(\kappa,\rho)^{5/4}\right].\]

The physical-parameter wrapper substitutes \(\kappa=M/m\), \(\eta=M_2/(m\sqrt m)\), and the literal source definition of \(\rho\). Its assumptions are positive strong convexity, \(m\le M\), a nonnegative Hessian Lipschitz bound, positive accuracy, and \(p\ge1\). No comparison between the condition numbers is hidden in those assumptions.

steps.title: Identify the additional regime in which the printed shape is valid
steps.body:
If the extra inequality \(\kappa\le\rho\) holds, the maximum in the corrected theorem equals \(\rho\), so the source's proposed shape is a valid upper bound with universal constant 64. The physical condition is exactly

\[M(1-p^{-1/3})\le M_2^{2/3}.\]

The equivalence follows by multiplying the original condition-number inequality by \(m>0\) and rearranging. This is a substantive extra regime, not a consequence of strong convexity or smoothness. The final wrapper makes that condition explicit and specializes the physical max theorem.

steps.title: Construct an exact family exposing the missing ordinary condition number
steps.body:
Take \(t>0\), \(\kappa=t^2\), \(\eta=1\), \(p=t^6\), and \(\varepsilon=1\). The exact fractional-power rules give \((t^6)^{-1/3}=t^{-2}\), so the source condition number is identically \(\rho=2\). Meanwhile the ordinary stability term alone implies \(\mathcal W\ge20\kappa^2=20t^4\). Its proposed simplification is at most \(8t^3\): \(\sqrt{t^6}=t^3\), \(2^{5/4}\le2^2=4\), and the two terms each cost at most \(4t^3\).

The proof therefore compares exact finite expressions, without relying on informal asymptotic notation. This is a counterexample to a scalar step/count simplification. It does not establish a lower bound on the possible performance of the stochastic algorithm.

steps.title: Rule out every uniform multiplicative repair of the printed formula
steps.body:
For any \(C>0\), choose a natural number \(n>C+1\). The preceding family has genuine integer dimension \(n^6\). Its proposed expression times \(C\) is at most \(8Cn^3\), which is strictly smaller than \(20n^4\), a lower bound on the actual reciprocal-step prescription. Hence no dimension-uniform constant \(C\) can turn the printed expression into a bound for this prescription over all admissible parameters.

The last theorem states the same contradiction with the literal physical definition \(\rho=(M_2^{2/3}+Mp^{-1/3})/m\), using \(m=M_2=1\), \(M=n^2\), and \(p=n^6\). The normalization identity identifies this physical expression with the already checked family. The conclusion concerns algebraic certification budgets; no stochastic complexity lower bound is asserted.
